natural: Rain over the Kirchberg plateau, the kind that hangs rather than falls. Not light yet. The fourth floor has been switched on since half past six.
plain: It is raining in Kirchberg. It is still dark outside. The lights on the fourth floor have been on since 06:30.

natural: Grace Hopper is standing at a desk that is not hers, reading over Marie Curie's shoulder. Nobody has told you why you were asked to come up.
plain: Grace Hopper stands behind Marie Curie and reads her screen. Nobody told you why you were asked to come to this floor.

natural: You are the Project Support Office. Sit there. Ten minutes, then tell me whether I am exaggerating.
plain: You work in the Project Support Office. Sit here. Watch for ten minutes. Then tell me if I am making this sound worse than it is.

natural: Exaggerating about what?
plain: About what?

natural: That is what the ten minutes are for.
plain: That is what the ten minutes are for.

natural: Disbursement instruction. Third tranche, two hundred and fifty million. Value date Monday.
plain: This is a disbursement instruction. It is the third part of a loan. The amount is 250 million euro. The money must be in the country's account on Monday.

natural: It exists here, in LOS. Complete. Checked. Signed. Now watch.
plain: The instruction is already in LOS, our lending system. It is complete, checked and signed. Now watch what I do next.

natural: She opens the treasury system beside it and starts typing. Not fast. Field, glance, field.
plain: She opens the treasury system next to it and types the same information again. She types slowly. One field, then a look at the first screen, then the next field.

natural: You are typing it again.
plain: You are typing the same information a second time.

natural: Twenty-two fields. Then a third time, into the payment gateway. Then the second officer reads all three against each other before the four o'clock cut-off.
plain: Twenty-two fields. Then I type them a third time, into the payment gateway. Then a second officer compares all three versions before the 16:00 deadline.

natural: And if he disagrees with you?
plain: What happens if he does not agree with you?

natural: Then one of us is wrong and we find out which. That is the control. A person. Reading.
plain: Then one of us made a mistake and we find out who. That check is the control. It is one person reading the work of another. We call it four eyes.

natural: About fourteen hundred fields a quarter. We counted them. Audit made us count them.
plain: About 1,400 fields every three months are typed again by hand. We counted them because the internal auditors asked us to.

natural: Two findings, I heard.
plain: I heard the auditors raised two findings.

natural: Segregation of duties is one. The trail is two. You can see what LOS holds this morning. You cannot always see who changed it, or when.
plain: Yes. The first finding is about who is allowed to do which step. The second is about the record of changes. You can see what LOS contains today. You cannot always see who changed it, or when.

natural: LOS was written in the EFSF era and extended every year since. Fourteen years. Three people in the building can read the parts that matter, and two of them are contractors.
plain: LOS was built in the EFSF period, fourteen years ago, and changed every year since. Only three people here can read its most important parts. Two of them are contractors.

natural: Instruction to value date. How long?
plain: How many days pass between the instruction and the day the money arrives?

natural: Five working days when nothing surprises us. Reconciliation afterwards, three more.
plain: Five working days if nothing goes wrong. After the payment, reconciliation takes three more days.

natural: And a new instrument means new code. The last one took nine months from decision to first disbursement.
plain: And a new lending product means new software. The last one took nine months from the decision to the first payment.

natural: If the Treaty reform finishes ratifying, the common backstop arrives as a new instrument.
plain: If the Treaty reform is approved by all member states, the common backstop will arrive as a new lending product.

natural: Italy has not ratified, so it is planned rather than live and everybody is comfortable. The day it stops being planned we will have weeks and we will need nine months.
plain: Italy has not approved the reform yet. So the backstop is only planned, not real, and nobody worries. On the day it becomes real we will have a few weeks, and we will need nine months.

natural: Sorry. Cut-off.
plain: Excuse me. I have to finish before the deadline.

natural: So what are you asking me for?
plain: What do you want from me?

natural: Nothing yet. I have half an hour of Florence tomorrow, and I wanted to be able to say I had shown this to somebody who does projects for a living.
plain: Nothing yet. I have thirty minutes with Florence Nightingale tomorrow. I wanted to be able to say that I showed this to a project professional.

natural: Show her the printout. She signs the exceptions every month. She has never once watched anybody type them.
plain: Show her the paper. She signs the exception reports every month. She has never watched anyone type the payment by hand.

natural: No project. No budget, no charter, no name, no team. A floor of people working around a problem, and a printout with twenty-two boxes on it.
plain: There is no project yet. No money, no charter, no name, no team. There is only a floor of people working around a problem, and a paper with twenty-two boxes on it.

natural: B4-12 seats eight and has one screen that gives everybody a green cast. Leonardo da Vinci is two floors down and joins by video anyway, because the room he wanted was taken.
plain: Room B4-12 has eight seats and one screen that makes everyone look green. Leonardo da Vinci works two floors below. He joins by video because the room he wanted was booked.

natural: Thirty minutes. Funding plan at three, and I am not moving it.
plain: You have thirty minutes. I have a funding meeting at 15:00 and I will not move it.

natural: Five working days to a value date. Three more to reconcile. Fourteen hundred fields a quarter, re-keyed by hand. Two audit findings, both sitting on LOS.
plain: It takes five working days to pay money out, and three more days to check the records. Every three months staff type 1,400 fields again by hand. There are two open audit findings, both about LOS.

natural: I have known that for two years.
plain: I have known all of that for two years.

natural: Leonardo's audio arrives about half a second after his mouth.
plain: On the video screen, Leonardo's sound arrives about half a second after his lips move.

natural: Four.
plain: Four years.

natural: What?
plain: Sorry, what?

natural: IT has known for four. Fourteen years old, and every new instrument is bespoke code.
plain: The IT division has known for four years. The system is fourteen years old, and every new lending product needs software written specially for it.

natural: Am I minuting this?
plain: Should I write official minutes of this meeting?

natural: There is nothing to minute. Write it in your own book.
plain: There is nothing official to record yet. Just take notes for yourself.

natural: So we buy something. There are three vendors in this market and I could name all three from memory.
plain: So we should buy a product. Three companies sell this kind of system, and I can name all three without looking.

natural: You could name them. Neither of us could yet say what we would be buying.
plain: You can name them. But neither you nor I can yet say what exactly we would be buying.

natural: One instruction, entered once. Loan agreement to disbursement to repayment schedule, with nobody retyping it. Instruments configured, not coded. Reconciliation the same day. The word for it is straight-through processing.
plain: One instruction, typed once. It travels from the loan agreement to the payment to the repayment schedule, and nobody types it again. New lending products are set up by configuration, not by new software. Records are checked the same day. The name for this is straight-through processing.

natural: Cost.
plain: What does it cost?

natural: Eight and a half. Give or take two.
plain: About eight and a half million euro. The real figure could be two million higher or lower.

natural: Two million.
plain: Two million euro either way.

natural: I would want six weeks with the payment gateway before I said anything firmer. It drops the value date if the instruction arrives after sixteen hundred, and nobody has ever written down why.
plain: I would need six weeks looking at the payment gateway before I gave you a firmer number. If an instruction arrives after 16:00, the gateway loses the value date, and nobody ever wrote down the reason.

natural: Has the house done anything like this before?
plain: Has this organisation done a project like this before?

natural: Collateral register replacement, three years ago. I can pull the Project-End Report. Two pages of lessons learned. One page is entirely about business experts promised part-time who delivered part of part-time.
plain: Yes. We replaced the collateral register three years ago. I can find the Project-End Report. It has two pages of lessons learned. One whole page is about business experts who were promised part-time and gave much less than that.

natural: That one will happen to us. Print it.
plain: That problem will happen to us too. Please print the report.

natural: Twelve minutes.
plain: You have twelve minutes left.

natural: Florence. Own this. Not supportive in corridors. Own it.
plain: Florence, I need you to own this project. Not just to say kind things about it in the corridor. Own it.

natural: Lending Operations pays for it, is blamed for it, and either gets the benefit or does not. Yes. I own it.
plain: My division pays for it. My division is blamed if it fails. My division gets the benefit, or gets nothing. Yes. I own it.

natural: Then IT provides. Whatever this turns out to be, my division builds it and I answer for what comes out of it.
plain: Then the IT division will provide the solution. Whatever we decide to build, my division builds it, and I answer for the result.

natural: Two names on a whiteboard with no document underneath them. Gantt writes them down anyway, in a notebook that is not an artefact of anything.
plain: Two names are now on the whiteboard, but no document exists under them. Gantt writes them in his own notebook, which is not an official project document.

natural: You do this professionally, apparently. What happens next?
plain: I am told this is your profession. What is the next step?

natural: One page I can read before three o'clock. Draft it over the weekend and I will look at it Monday.
plain: One page that I can read before 15:00. Write it this weekend and I will read it on Monday.

natural: With what? A photograph of a whiteboard. He would ask what he is buying and I would have nothing at all to hand him.
plain: With what document? A photo of a whiteboard. He would ask what he is paying for, and I would have nothing to give him.

natural: Six weeks of whose time, on whose authority? Nothing has been approved. You would be spending a budget that does not exist.
plain: Six weeks of whose working time, approved by whom? Nothing has been approved yet. You would be spending money that has not been given to you.

natural: Kick-off for what? There is no charter to kick off and no team to invite.
plain: The start of what? There is no charter yet, and there is no team to invite.

natural: Monday. Sleet that cannot commit. Grace's office holds two chairs, a wall of loan files and a screen with an empty template on it.
plain: It is Monday. Wet snow is falling. Grace Hopper's office has two chairs, a wall of loan files, and a screen showing an empty template.

natural: Three o'clock. One page. She said one page and she meant one page.
plain: The deadline is 15:00. One page. Florence said one page and she meant it.

natural: What is it called?
plain: What is the project called?

natural: CASTOR. Renewal of the Lending Operations System. A castor is a beaver. It builds things and it works at night. The name is provisional, and everything provisional survives forever.
plain: CASTOR. The full title is Renewal of the Lending Operations System. A castor is a beaver. It builds things and it works at night. The name is temporary, and temporary names usually last for ever.

natural: Leonardo's estimate arrives at 09:12. Three thousand one hundred person-days. Around eight point four million all in. Twenty-six months. He has written the word indicative twice.
plain: Leonardo's estimate arrives by email at 09:12. It says 3,100 person-days, about 8.4 million euro in total, and 26 months. He wrote the word indicative twice, meaning it is only a rough figure.

natural: Type of delivery. In-house, outsourced, mix, or not known.
plain: Next box: type of delivery. The choices are in-house, outsourced, a mix of both, or not known yet.

natural: Mix. In-house core team, outsourced platform implementation.
plain: A mix. Our own core team, and an outside company to install and configure the platform.

natural: Florence puts her head round the door on her way to something else and does not come in.
plain: Florence looks in through the door on her way somewhere else. She does not come into the room.

natural: Fifteenth of May 2028. Write it down.
plain: The delivery date is 15 May 2028. Write that down.

natural: That is a need, not a promise.
plain: That is what you need, not what we promise.

natural: Write it down.
plain: Write it down anyway.

natural: It goes in as a target delivery date. The day it becomes a promise there will be a Charter under it.
plain: I will write it in the box called target delivery date. It becomes a promise only when a Project Charter supports it.

natural: Success criteria. Five days to one. Three days to same day. Nine months to six weeks. Two open findings to zero.
plain: Now the success criteria. Paying out: from five working days to one. Reconciliation: from three days to the same day. Adding a new lending product: from nine months to six weeks. Open audit findings: from two to zero.

natural: Not the fourteen hundred fields?
plain: Should we not also include the 1,400 re-typed fields?

natural: Business Case, with Ada's process map under it. High level here, or the page becomes four pages and nobody reads any of them.
plain: That belongs in the Business Case, with Ada Lovelace's process map to support it. This document stays at a high level. Otherwise one page becomes four and nobody reads any of them.

natural: Risks.
plain: What about the risks?

natural: Ratification. The backstop stays a planned capability rather than a live one, so the scope can move under us.
plain: The main risk is ratification. The common backstop is only planned, not yet real. So the size of the job can change while we work.

natural: Do not put Italy in a document that goes to the Investment Board.
plain: Do not name Italy in a document that goes to the Corporate Investment Board.

natural: It is in the public ratification table. He can read it there, or he can read it from us.
plain: The information is already public, in the official ratification table. Lorenzo can read it there, or he can read it in our document.

natural: Johannes Gutenberg is in the doorway holding a printout nobody asked him for.
plain: Johannes Gutenberg stands in the doorway. He is holding a printed page that nobody asked him to bring.

natural: Before anybody signs anything. Where does this live? Version 1.0, project folder, document location filled in. Not an attachment in three mailboxes with three different dates on it.
plain: Before anyone signs: where will this document be stored? Mark it version 1.0, put it in the project folder, and fill in the document location box. It must not exist as an email attachment in three mailboxes with three different dates.

natural: Hello, Johannes. You did not say hello.
plain: Hello, Johannes. You started talking without saying hello.

natural: I could accept this myself and we would be finished by lunch.
plain: I could approve this document myself, and we would be finished before lunch.

natural: For a smaller request, yes. At eight point four million the approving authority is the Corporate Investment Board, chaired by Lorenzo de' Medici.
plain: For a smaller request, yes. At 8.4 million euro the approver is the Corporate Investment Board, which Lorenzo de' Medici chairs.

natural: And it does not ask him for eight point four million. It asks him to let us spend six weeks finding out whether eight point four is the right number.
plain: And the document does not ask him for 8.4 million euro. It asks him to let us spend six weeks finding out whether 8.4 million is the right figure.

natural: Then somebody write it.
plain: Then one of you write it.

natural: Then sit down. There are four boxes I cannot fill without you. Type of delivery, effort, approving authority, and what actually happens after they say yes.
plain: Then sit down. I cannot fill in four boxes without you: type of delivery, effort, who approves it, and what happens after they agree.

natural: You could. Then the one document that says what Lending Operations needs would be written by somebody who has never made a disbursement.
plain: You could. Then the only document describing what Lending Operations needs would be written by a person who has never paid money out.

natural: It is not Leonardo's system. It is my division's process. If IT writes the request, the Investment Board will ask why the business did not.
plain: The system is not Leonardo's. The process is my division's. If IT writes the request, the Corporate Investment Board will ask why the business did not write it.

natural: Same words, different document. If I only sign it, then when Lorenzo asks me why the target date is May, I will be reading my own page to find out.
plain: The words would be the same, but the document would not. If I only sign it, then when Lorenzo asks me why the date is May, I will have to read my own page to find the answer.

natural: A1-02 is the good room. Working screen, working microphones, a table for twenty-two. Lorenzo de' Medici chairs. There are nine items this morning. CASTOR is item seven and has eleven minutes.
plain: Room A1-02 is the best room. The screen works, the microphones work, and the table seats twenty-two. Lorenzo de' Medici is the chair. There are nine items today. CASTOR is item seven and has eleven minutes.

natural: One page. Thank you for the one page. Most people bring me forty and hope.
plain: One page. Thank you for keeping it to one page. Most people bring forty pages and hope for the best.

natural: Fourteen-year-old system, two open audit findings, three thousand one hundred person-days, eight point four million, twenty-six months, delivery mix. Florence. Before you begin. What am I approving?
plain: A fourteen-year-old system. Two open audit findings. 3,100 person-days, 8.4 million euro, 26 months, mixed delivery. Florence, before you start: what exactly am I approving?

natural: The replacement of a system that is —
plain: You are approving the replacement of a system that is...

natural: No. What am I approving today?
plain: No. What am I approving today, in this meeting?

natural: Authority to write a Business Case. Not the money, not a platform, not a supplier.
plain: Permission to write a Business Case. Not the money, not a product, not a supplier.

natural: Good. If I released eight point four million against a page and a half, the Board of Directors would be entitled to ask what I am for.
plain: Good. If I released 8.4 million euro on the basis of one and a half pages, the Board of Directors could reasonably ask why my committee exists.

natural: And for the Board, in one sentence: this is administrative budget. It does not touch the lending capacity and it does not touch paid-in capital. Somebody always asks.
plain: And for the Board of Directors, in one sentence: this money comes from our own running costs. It does not reduce how much we can lend, and it does not touch the paid-in capital. Somebody always asks that question.

natural: Second question, and you will keep hearing it from me. The envelope was allocated in October. Nothing in this room is free. What leaves the portfolio to make room?
plain: Second question, and I will ask it every time. The investment budget was shared out in October. Nothing here is free. What comes out of the portfolio to make space for this?

natural: The audit findings do not leave. They are already ours, and they get older.
plain: The audit findings will not go away. They are already our problem, and they get older every year.

natural: That is an argument for doing it. It is not an answer to the question I asked.
plain: That is a reason to do the project. It is not an answer to my question.

natural: You could slip the reporting warehouse refresh by twelve months.
plain: You could delay the reporting warehouse upgrade by twelve months.

natural: I would rather you had not heard that from me.
plain: I would prefer that you had not heard that suggestion from me.

natural: I will hear it from the Business Case, costed, with the consequence written next to it. In March. Not today.
plain: I will hear it from the Business Case, with a price and with the consequence written beside it. In March. Not today.

natural: Nobody else writes that down. You write it down.
plain: Nobody else in the room writes that instruction down. You do.

natural: You, at the end, with the pen. You are not on my list.
plain: You, at the end of the table, with the pen. Your name is not on my attendance list.

natural: Project Support Office. Carrying the folder and taking the notes nobody else is taking.
plain: I am from the Project Support Office. I carry the file and I take the notes that nobody else is taking.

natural: Then take them accurately. In March that page is the difference between a decision and a preference.
plain: Then take them accurately. In March, that page will decide whether we have a real decision or only an opinion.

natural: Who sits on your steering committee?
plain: Who are the members of your steering committee?

natural: There is no steering committee. There is no project.
plain: There is no steering committee. There is no project yet.

natural: Then assemble a preliminary one before the Business Case reaches me. I would like somebody who understands lending to have read it before I do.
plain: Then set up a first version of one before the Business Case comes to me. I want someone who understands lending to read it before I do.

natural: Leonardo. Project Manager?
plain: Leonardo, who will be the Project Manager?

natural: After the Business Case. I have somebody in mind.
plain: I will appoint one after the Business Case is approved. I already have someone in mind.

natural: Item seven carries at 11:14. The Project Initiation Request of 12 January is approved and the Board moves to item eight, which is about bicycle parking.
plain: Item seven is approved at 11:14. The Project Initiation Request of 12 January is accepted. The committee moves to item eight, which is about bicycle parking.

natural: You leave A1-02 with authority to spend six weeks. The project still does not exist.
plain: You leave room A1-02 with permission to spend six weeks of work. The project still does not formally exist.

natural: The file room has no window and the best whiteboard on the floor. Ada Lovelace has taped six process maps to a cabinet and numbered them in the corner.
plain: The file room has no window and the best whiteboard on the floor. Ada Lovelace has taped six process diagrams to a cupboard and numbered each one in the corner.

natural: Forty-one steps from signed loan agreement to value date. Nine of them exist only because two systems cannot speak to each other.
plain: There are 41 steps between the signed loan agreement and the day the money arrives. Nine of those steps exist only because two systems cannot exchange data.

natural: Step thirty-one. The back office telephones treasury to confirm the nostro is funded. Telephones.
plain: Look at step 31. The back office telephones the treasury team to confirm that the nostro account has enough money. By telephone.

natural: That is 2.2, current situation impact. It stays, with the number on it.
plain: That belongs in section 2.2, the impact of the current situation. It stays in the document, with the figure attached.

natural: Before you bury B, let me defend it.
plain: Before you throw away option B, let me argue for it.

natural: Nobody is burying anything.
plain: Nobody is throwing anything away.

natural: We re-platform LOS and extend it. The knowledge stays in this building. And nothing you buy will do our value-date logic. Nothing.
plain: Option B is to rebuild LOS on new technology and extend it. The knowledge stays inside this organisation. And no product you can buy will handle our value-date rules correctly. None of them.

natural: Which problem does that solve?
plain: Which problem does option B solve?

natural: Continuity.
plain: It keeps things running as they are.

natural: The problem on the wall is bespoke code for every instrument. B keeps it.
plain: The problem written on the wall is that every new lending product needs software written specially for it. Option B does not remove that.

natural: B keeps it cheaper.
plain: Option B keeps that problem, but at a lower price.

natural: Then that is B's weakness, it goes in B's SWOT, and B stays in the document. It is a real option. It is simply not the recommendation.
plain: Then that is the weakness of option B. It goes in the SWOT table for option B, and option B stays in the document. It is a real option. It is just not the one we recommend.

natural: Nikola, you are here on framework days. Everything you have seen this week goes in the tender file, so every bidder gets it.
plain: Nikola, you are working here under an existing framework contract. Everything you have seen this week will be added to the tender file, so that every company that bids receives the same information.

natural: Naturally. Levallois will bid.
plain: Of course. My company, Levallois Systems, will bid for the work.

natural: Which is exactly why it goes in the file.
plain: That is exactly why the information must go in the file for everyone.

natural: And A is do nothing. A is always in there. Keep LOS, spend nothing, both findings stay open, onboarding stays at nine months. Written out honestly, it argues against itself.
plain: And option A is to do nothing. Option A is always included. Keep LOS, spend no money, leave both audit findings open, and keep the nine months needed for a new product. If you write it honestly, it defeats itself.

natural: Florence comes in with her coat still on and does not sit down.
plain: Florence comes in. She is still wearing her coat and she does not sit down.

natural: Where are we?
plain: How far have you got?

natural: Alternative C. Configure a market platform, delivered as a mix. Eight point four million, twenty-six months. The five-year total cost of ownership adds licence, maintenance, support and training, and that is the number Lorenzo will actually read.
plain: We recommend option C: buy a lending platform from the market and configure it, with a mix of our own staff and an outside company. It costs 8.4 million euro over 26 months. The five-year total cost of ownership also adds licence, maintenance, support and training. That is the number Lorenzo will really look at.

natural: And his question.
plain: And what about his question, on the trade-off?

natural: 5.12. Synergies and interdependencies. Still empty. Leave it empty and he will fill it in for you, out loud, in the meeting.
plain: Section 5.12, on links with other projects, is still empty. If you leave it empty, Lorenzo will answer it himself, out loud, in the meeting.

natural: Who is going to count fourteen hundred fields in 2028?
plain: In 2028, who will count 1,400 fields to check whether we succeeded?

natural: The same two people who counted them in December. It took a morning.
plain: The same two people who counted them in December. It took one morning.

natural: Then let me tell you what I actually want. Three vendors, one tender, published mid-March. Two months saved.
plain: Now let me tell you what I really want. Three suppliers, one tender, published in the middle of March. That saves two months.

natural: That would put procurement in front of —
plain: That would put the tender before the...

natural: Every month spent writing up options we did not choose is a month those findings stay open. You are the process person. Tell me why I cannot.
plain: Every month we spend describing options we did not choose is another month those audit findings stay open. You are the methodology person. Tell me why I cannot do it.

natural: And when it comes out as C anyway, it will have cost me six weeks. Fine. Write it. But 5.12 had better be full by the tenth.
plain: And when the answer is option C anyway, it will have cost me six weeks. All right. Write it. But section 5.12 must be complete by the tenth.

natural: That is what you do when the project exists because somebody won a bid. We are the ones deciding whether to hold one.
plain: You do that when the project exists only because a supplier won a tender. Here we are still deciding whether to hold a tender at all.

natural: Kindly, no. I am Responsible for this document and Florence is Accountable for it. You support it. The day the Board asks whose numbers these are, the honest answer would be the wrong one.
plain: No, thank you. I am Responsible for this document and Florence is Accountable for it. You support us. If the Board asked whose figures these were, the true answer would be the wrong answer.

natural: Then it is not a Business Case. It is a purchase order with an essay attached. Comparing things is that committee's entire job.
plain: Then it is not a Business Case. It is an order form with a long explanation attached. Comparing options is the only job that committee has.

natural: Nine people in a room built for eight. Lorenzo de' Medici joins by video for the first fifteen minutes. The green cast makes him look unwell, which he is not.
plain: Nine people are in a room with eight seats. Lorenzo de' Medici joins by video for the first fifteen minutes. The screen's green light makes him look ill. He is not ill.

natural: I am told I chair this. Somebody tell me what this is.
plain: I am told that I chair this meeting. Somebody please tell me what this meeting is.

natural: A preliminary Project Steering Committee. Four permanent seats. Project Owner, Solution Provider, Business Manager, Project Manager. The rest of us are here because the project needs us.
plain: It is a first Project Steering Committee. It has four permanent seats: Project Owner, Solution Provider, Business Manager and Project Manager. The rest of us attend because the project needs us.

natural: I am Quality Assurance. This committee assigns me, and I do not report to the Project Manager.
plain: I am Project Quality Assurance. This committee appoints me, and I do not report to the Project Manager.

natural: And I am here because somebody has finally asked the people who do the typing.
plain: And I am here because somebody has finally asked the staff who type the payments.

natural: Architecture Office. I advise. I do not vote. And I would like the configuration engine demonstrated before anybody commits to release two.
plain: I am from the Architecture Office. I give advice. I do not vote. And I would like to see the configuration engine working before anyone commits to release two.

natural: Then we approve the Business Case this morning.
plain: Then this committee will approve the Business Case this morning.

natural: This committee is consulted on the Business Case. It is accountable for the Charter. Different rows. It will matter in a fortnight.
plain: This committee is only consulted on the Business Case. It is accountable for the Project Charter. Those are two different lines in the table. The difference will matter in two weeks.

natural: So who approves it?
plain: Then who approves the Business Case?

natural: You do, as Project Owner. Then you send it up, because of the amount.
plain: You do, as Project Owner. Then you send it upward to the Corporate Investment Board, because of the amount of money involved.

natural: Which brings me to the page I asked for in January.
plain: That brings me to the page I asked for in January.

natural: 5.12 is no longer empty. The reporting warehouse refresh slips from 2026 into 2027. The cost of the slip is priced on the same page. Two quarters of manual regulatory extracts. About ninety person-days of Finance and Control time.
plain: Section 5.12 is no longer empty. The reporting warehouse upgrade moves from 2026 to 2027. The cost of that delay is priced on the same page: six months of producing regulatory reports by hand, about 90 person-days of work in Finance and Control.

natural: Leonardo. Is that survivable?
plain: Leonardo, can your division live with that?

natural: It is survivable. It is not free. And I want it written down that I said so, because in November somebody will ask why the extracts are late.
plain: We can live with it. It is not free. And I want my words recorded, because in November somebody will ask why the reports are late.

natural: It is written down. That is what the page is for. Florence, that is what I meant in January. Not a sacrifice. A decision, with the price beside it.
plain: It is recorded. That is the purpose of the page. Florence, that is what I meant in January. Not a sacrifice, but a decision with its price written next to it.

natural: Lorenzo leaves the call at 10:16. The room breathes out.
plain: Lorenzo leaves the video call at 10:16. The people in the room relax.

natural: May I say the unpopular thing. Nobody has asked my forty administrators what they need. You have written a business case about them.
plain: May I say something unwelcome. Nobody has asked my forty loan administrators what they need. You have written a business case about them, not with them.

natural: You are right, and that is the next document, not this one. This one had to establish whether the money exists.
plain: You are right. That belongs in the next document, not this one. This document only had to establish whether the money exists.

natural: Next document. I am writing that down.
plain: The next document. I am writing that promise down.

natural: Leonardo. If the Investment Board says yes on the twenty-fourth, who runs this?
plain: Leonardo, if the Corporate Investment Board agrees on the twenty-fourth, who will manage this project?

natural: I was going to do that in April.
plain: I was planning to appoint someone in April.

natural: Do it now.
plain: Appoint someone now.

natural: Then it is the one who has been carrying the folder since January.
plain: Then it is the person who has been carrying the project file since January.

natural: He means you. It is not ceremonial. From this moment the Project Charter is yours to deliver, and the Business Case never will be.
plain: He means you. This is not a formality. From now on you must deliver the Project Charter. The Business Case will never be yours.

natural: Then I need the Business Case final on Friday. The Charter has to quote its success criteria, not paraphrase them.
plain: Then I need the final Business Case on Friday. The Charter must copy its success criteria exactly, not describe them in different words.

natural: Congratulations. You now have fourteen days and a document.
plain: Congratulations. You now have fourteen days and one document to produce.

natural: You have the pen now. It is a different weight from carrying the folder.
plain: You are now writing the document yourself. That feels different from only carrying the file.

natural: I drafted section 2 and I have talked to everybody this touches. From here it is yours, and my job is to support you.
plain: I wrote section 2 and I have spoken to everyone affected. From now on the document is yours. My job is to support you.

natural: Scope statement. Replace LOS with a configurable lending operations platform delivering straight-through processing from loan agreement to disbursement and repayment schedule.
plain: Here is the scope statement. Replace LOS with a lending platform that can be configured, and that moves data automatically from the loan agreement to the payment and the repayment schedule.

natural: Say the out-of-scope loudly. People hear new system and assume treasury goes too. Then they assume their own thing goes with it.
plain: Say clearly what is not included. When people hear new system, they assume the treasury system is included too. Then they assume their own system is included as well.

natural: Out of scope: the treasury system. Out of scope: the payment messaging gateway. Out of scope: bespoke screens for the SRF backstop.
plain: Not included: the treasury system. Not included: the payment messaging gateway. Not included: specially built screens for the SRF backstop.

natural: Backstop out? Somebody will ask about that.
plain: The backstop is excluded? Somebody will certainly ask about that.

natural: The backstop arrives as configuration, if it arrives. That is precisely how we stop the project being hostage to a ratification nobody in this building controls.
plain: If the backstop arrives, it will be set up by configuration, not by new software. That is how we stop the project depending on a ratification that nobody here can control.

natural: Does it process personal data?
plain: Will the new system process personal data?

natural: Staff identifiers in the audit trail. Counterparty contact details.
plain: Yes. Staff identity numbers in the audit trail, and the contact details of the other party to each deal.

natural: Then your beautiful audit trail is also a processing operation. I want that in the constraints in March, not discovered by me in June.
plain: Then your excellent audit trail is also an operation that processes personal data. I want that written in the constraints section in March. I do not want to discover it myself in June.

natural: And four eyes has to survive the automation.
plain: And the four-eyes check must still work after the process is automated.

natural: Meaning?
plain: What do you mean exactly?

natural: If straight-through means one officer can originate and release the same disbursement, you have closed one audit finding and opened a worse one.
plain: If automatic processing lets one officer both create and send the same payment, you have closed one audit finding and created a worse one.

natural: Then it is a feature in 3.5, in scope, traced to a deliverable. Not a footnote.
plain: Then it becomes a feature in section 3.5. It is in scope and linked to a deliverable. It is not a small note at the bottom of a page.

natural: Put the architect risk in as well. R-07, loss of the contractor's key architect. High and high. Named-staff clause, documented knowledge transfer. Write it in March and procurement can price it in September.
plain: Add the architect risk too. It is R-07: losing the contractor's main architect. Likelihood high, impact high. The answer is a contract clause naming the staff, and written handover of knowledge. If we write it in March, the buyers can put a price on it in September.

natural: Cost, 4.1. Eight point four million across 2026 to 2028, three thousand one hundred person-days internal, type of delivery mix.
plain: Section 4.1, cost. 8.4 million euro from 2026 to 2028, 3,100 person-days of our own effort, and a mixed type of delivery.

natural: Milestones, 4.2. Ready for Executing the third of July, contract award the eighteenth of September, release one March 2027, release two December 2027, parallel run January to April 2028, go-live the fifteenth of May.
plain: Section 4.2, milestones. Ready for Executing on 3 July. Contract awarded on 18 September. Release 1 in March 2027. Release 2 in December 2027. Parallel run from January to April 2028. Go-live on 15 May 2028.

natural: And 5.1 says PM², no deviations. Shortest paragraph in the document, and the one people will argue about longest.
plain: And section 5.1 says we use the PM² method with no changes. It is the shortest paragraph in the document, and the one people will argue about for the longest time.

natural: Ada comes in with a ring binder that will not close.
plain: Ada Lovelace comes in carrying a large folder that is too full to close.

natural: Two hundred and twelve requirements. Six workshops. Marie's people signed every sheet.
plain: There are 212 requirements, from six workshops. Marie Curie's staff signed every page.

natural: Every one of those is somebody's actual working day. They go in.
plain: Each of those requirements is part of somebody's real working day. They must be included.

natural: Two hundred and twelve, in a document meant to be read in twenty minutes by people who do not work on this floor.
plain: That is 212 items, in a document that people from other floors are supposed to read in twenty minutes.

natural: They do not go in the Charter. The Charter carries high-level needs and features and points at them. They go in a Requirements Document, referenced in appendix one, and we elaborate them in planning.
plain: They do not go inside the Charter. The Charter holds high-level needs and features, and refers to the detail. The 212 items go in a Requirements Document, named in appendix one, and we work on them in the Planning Phase.

natural: Then reference it properly, with a document location. If it lives on my drive it does not exist.
plain: Then refer to it correctly, with the storage location written in. If it only exists on my own drive, it does not exist at all.

natural: As long as pointing at them is not a polite way of forgetting them.
plain: That is acceptable, as long as referring to them is not a polite way of forgetting them.

natural: It is not. You review them and you sign them off, and that is written into section 6 with your name against it.
plain: It is not. You will review them and sign them off. That is written in section 6 of the Charter, with your name next to it.

natural: Henry Gantt has produced an agenda with numbered items and a decision column. The video kit is switched off. For once everybody is in the room.
plain: Henry Gantt has prepared an agenda with numbered items and a column for decisions. The video equipment is off. For once, everyone is physically in the room.

natural: Attendance for the record. Project Owner, Solution Provider, Business Manager, Project Manager, User Representative, Architecture Office, Quality Assurance. Item one, Business Case version 1.0. Item two, Project Charter version 1.0.
plain: For the record, those present are: the Project Owner, the Solution Provider, the Business Manager, the Project Manager, the User Representative, the Architecture Office and Quality Assurance. Item one is the Business Case version 1.0. Item two is the Project Charter version 1.0.

natural: I am at Lorenzo's table at two. I would like to arrive with something signed.
plain: I am at Lorenzo's committee at 14:00 today. I would like to arrive with a signed document.

natural: Marie.
plain: Marie, please start.

natural: I have read both. The Charter says my people are a deliverable. D-04, forty staff trained. First time in fourteen years training has been on the same list as software.
plain: I have read both documents. The Charter treats my staff as a deliverable: D-04, forty people trained. In fourteen years this is the first time training appears on the same list as software.

natural: So I will not complain about the rest today.
plain: So today I will not complain about anything else.

natural: Architecture supports C, on condition the configuration engine is demonstrated before release two is committed. The condition is in the Charter. I am satisfied.
plain: The Architecture Office supports option C, on one condition: the configuration engine must be demonstrated before release two is committed. That condition is written in the Charter, so I am satisfied.

natural: Quality Assurance. I reviewed the Charter against the Business Case. Two non-conformities. Both closed on Friday.
plain: Quality Assurance. I compared the Charter with the Business Case. I found two places where they did not match. Both were corrected on Friday.

natural: Which two?
plain: Which two problems?

natural: The reconciliation target in 3.2 had drifted to next day. And the risk table had no owners in it.
plain: First, the reconciliation target in section 3.2 had changed to next day instead of same day. Second, the risk table had no named owners.

natural: Drifted.
plain: It changed by itself?

natural: Somebody copied an old table. It is corrected. Same day, not next day. Two documents, one baseline. That is the reason Deming reads it and I do not review my own document.
plain: Someone copied an old version of the table. It has been corrected: same day, not next day. The two documents now form one baseline. That is why Deming checks the document and I do not review my own work.

natural: Cost and effort confirmed as they stand. The tender is planning work. It is not in front of you this morning.
plain: The cost and effort figures are confirmed as written. Running the tender is work for the Planning Phase. It is not being decided this morning.

natural: The Business Implementation Group has read both. Lending Operations, Finance and Control, Risk, Legal. Legal wants a paragraph on contract templates, and that belongs in planning.
plain: The Business Implementation Group has read both documents. It includes Lending Operations, Finance and Control, Risk and Legal. Legal wants a paragraph about contract templates, and that belongs in the Planning Phase.

natural: Objections? None. Good.
plain: Are there any objections? No. Good.

natural: She turns the Charter over to the last page, where the signature block is, and takes out a pen.
plain: She turns the Charter to the last page, where the signature block is, and takes out a pen.

natural: Where do I sign?
plain: Where do I sign?

natural: Gantt's pen stops moving. Deming looks at you. So does Grace.
plain: Gantt stops writing. Deming looks at you. Grace looks at you as well.

natural: That depends what you think you are doing.
plain: That depends on what you believe you are doing.

natural: Florence —
plain: Florence, wait...

natural: I am the Project Owner, I am paying for it, and I have read it twice. Where is the difficulty?
plain: I am the Project Owner. My division pays for this. I have read the document twice. What is the problem?

natural: So I do it twice. Once here, and once at Lorenzo's table this afternoon. Accepted, then. Gantt, minute it as a committee decision.
plain: So I do it twice: once here, and once at Lorenzo's committee this afternoon. Very well, it is accepted. Gantt, record it as a decision of the committee.

natural: Then this committee has just watched its chair approve a document to herself.
plain: Then this committee has just watched its own chair approve a document to herself.

natural: Responsible for delivering it. Not accountable for accepting it. Two different letters, and never the same person.
plain: You are responsible for producing it. You are not accountable for accepting it. Those are two different letters, and never the same person.

natural: Then Lorenzo accepts a charter that nobody who actually works on this project has ever accepted, and the first time we escalate an issue he will ask why we did not settle it here.
plain: Then Lorenzo accepts a charter that nobody working on the project has accepted. The first time we send him a problem, he will ask why we did not solve it in our own committee.

natural: On the afternoon of the twenty-fourth Florence carried both documents to the Corporate Investment Board. It approved the Business Case and gave corporate approval to the Charter in nineteen minutes, most of which were about the reporting warehouse.
plain: On the afternoon of 24 March, Florence took both documents to the Corporate Investment Board. The Board approved the Business Case and gave corporate approval of the Charter in nineteen minutes. Most of that time was spent on the reporting warehouse.

natural: Three days later the same people are back in B4-12 and there is a spreadsheet on the screen.
plain: Three days later the same people are back in room B4-12. There is a spreadsheet on the screen.

natural: We approved everything on Tuesday. What is this?
plain: We approved everything on Tuesday. What is this meeting for?

natural: The gate. Ready for Planning. Tuesday's question was whether the documents are approved. Today's question is whether we are in a fit state to start planning.
plain: This is the gate called Ready for Planning. On Tuesday the question was whether the documents were approved. Today the question is whether we are ready to start planning.

natural: Twenty-eight questions on one sheet, and the Project Manager answers every one of them before asking this committee for anything.
plain: There are 28 questions on one sheet. The Project Manager answers all of them before asking this committee for anything.

natural: Question twenty-one. Logs.
plain: Question 21, about the project logs.

natural: Risk, Issue and Decision, all open. Nine risks, R-07 among them. Two issues. Four decisions, including the reporting warehouse slip. The Change Log we open in planning.
plain: The Risk Log, the Issue Log and the Decision Log are all open. There are nine risks, including R-07. There are two issues. There are four decisions, including the delay to the reporting warehouse. The Change Log will be opened during planning.

natural: Twenty-four. Security, document management, data protection.
plain: Question 24, about security, document management and data protection.

natural: Turing and Brandeis have both signed their sections. Johannes has the repository and the naming convention, so the Charter and the Business Case sit in one place with version numbers.
plain: Alan Turing and Louis Brandeis have both signed their sections. Johannes Gutenberg has set up the document store and the naming rules, so the Charter and the Business Case are in one place with version numbers.

natural: Sixteen and twenty-five. Business Case approved. Charter accepted by this committee. Both Tuesday, both minuted.
plain: Questions 16 and 25. The Business Case is approved. The Charter was accepted by this committee. Both happened on Tuesday and both are in the minutes.

natural: Twelve to fifteen. Total cost of ownership in euro and in full-time equivalents, both sides costed, funding lines named, savings estimated. That took the longest, and it is the part Lorenzo will reuse in October.
plain: Questions 12 to 15. The total cost of ownership is given in euro and in full-time equivalents. The costs of both the business side and the IT side are included. The budget lines are named and the savings are estimated. That work took the longest, and Lorenzo will use it again in October.

natural: And if the answer to one of these had been no?
plain: And what would happen if the answer to one of these questions was no?

natural: Then it is not a delay.
plain: Then it would not simply be a delay.

natural: If the Business Case or the Charter is not approved, the project goes directly to Closing. Lessons learned, archive the folder, everybody back to their division.
plain: If the Business Case or the Charter is not approved, the project moves straight to the Closing Phase. You collect the lessons learned, store the documents, and everyone returns to their own division.

natural: Florence does not answer that, which is itself an answer.
plain: Florence says nothing in reply. Her silence is itself a kind of answer.

natural: Is there anything on that sheet you cannot tick?
plain: Is there any question on that sheet that you cannot answer yes to?

natural: One.
plain: One question.

natural: Question nine, on the screen: were at least four alternatives analysed?
plain: Question 9 is on the screen. It asks whether at least four alternative solutions were analysed.

natural: We analysed three. Do nothing, extend LOS, configure a market platform. There was no credible fourth and I am not going to invent one.
plain: We analysed three options: do nothing, extend LOS, and configure a platform bought from the market. There was no realistic fourth option, and I will not invent one.

natural: The sheet says four. The sheet is a spreadsheet, not a treaty.
plain: The sheet asks for four. But the sheet is only a spreadsheet. It is not a legal text.

natural: The Initiating sheet comes out at ninety-six per cent. What does one question cost us?
plain: The Initiating sheet scores 96 per cent. What does this one question cost us?

natural: That depends entirely on what I type in the box.
plain: That depends completely on what I write in the answer box.

natural: Three options, one of them do nothing, and Lorenzo's board took it on Tuesday. Noted, accepted, and written down. Gantt, planning kick-off, the ninth of April.
plain: Three options, and one of them was to do nothing. Lorenzo's board accepted that on Tuesday. It is noted, accepted and recorded. Gantt, book the planning kick-off for 9 April.

natural: Then the first inaccurate answer in the workbook is on the line that matters, and everything under it is worth less. I would find it at the Planning gate in any case.
plain: Then the first wrong answer in the workbook sits on the line that matters most, and every answer below it is worth less. I would find it at the next gate anyway.

natural: A fourth option invented to satisfy a spreadsheet is worse than three real ones, and it costs us the kick-off and the procurement slot behind it.
plain: A fourth option invented only to satisfy a spreadsheet is worse than three real ones. It would also cost us the kick-off date and the procurement slot that follows it.

natural: It is your tool, and it also sits in the project folder for the next six years. N/A means the question does not apply. It applied.
plain: It is your tool, and it will also stay in the project folder for six years. Not Applicable means the question does not apply to this project. This question did apply.

natural: Twenty-one people, one room, 09:30 to 12:30. The agenda went out on the second of April with the Charter attached, and at 09:34 four of them are reading it for the first time. Legal are on video from the fourth floor, on the camera that has pointed at the ceiling tiles since the EFSF migration.
plain: Twenty-one people are in one room, booked from 09:30 to 12:30. The agenda was sent on 2 April with the Project Charter attached. At 09:34, four people are reading it for the first time. Legal join by video from the fourth floor, on the camera that has pointed at the ceiling tiles since the EFSF migration.

natural: Notes or minutes?
plain: Do you want me to take informal notes, or official minutes?

natural: Minutes. And mark the actions while you hear them, because I will lose four of them by eleven.
plain: Official minutes. Please write down each action item as you hear it. If you wait, I will forget about four of them by 11:00.

natural: Then I record who is here. Not who was invited. Finance and Control have sent a deputy and I do not have her name.
plain: Then I will record the people who are actually present, not the people who were invited. Finance and Control sent a deputy, and I do not know her name.

natural: Names first. Each of you, one sentence on what CASTOR changes about your Tuesday.
plain: We start with introductions. Please each say your name and one sentence about how CASTOR will change your normal working Tuesday.

natural: Twenty-one sentences.
plain: That will be twenty-one sentences.

natural: Fifteen minutes. It is the cheapest fifteen minutes of the morning.
plain: It will take fifteen minutes. It is the most useful fifteen minutes we will spend today.

natural: It takes nineteen. A tester from IT says CASTOR will change nothing about his Tuesday, which turns out to be the most useful sentence anybody says before the break.
plain: It takes nineteen minutes. A tester from the IT division says CASTOR will change nothing about his Tuesday. That turns out to be the most useful sentence anyone says before the break.

natural: Fourteen years old. Fourteen hundred payment fields re-keyed by hand every quarter. Three working days to reconcile a disbursement. Two open audit findings with my signature on the response to both.
plain: The LOS system is fourteen years old. Staff retype 1,400 payment fields by hand every three months. Checking the records after a payment takes three working days. There are two open audit findings, and I signed the reply to both.

natural: I am not here for a nicer system. I am here to stop writing those responses.
plain: I do not want a nicer system. I want to stop writing replies to audit findings.

natural: Charter, line by line. Scope. SC1 to SC5. Eight point four million, three thousand one hundred person-days, twenty-six months, go-live the fifteenth of May 2028.
plain: Now I go through the Project Charter line by line. The scope. The five success criteria. The budget of 8.4 million euro, the 3,100 person-days of effort, the 26 months, and the go-live date of 15 May 2028.

natural: Stop at SC1. Five working days down to one. Those five days are not idle. Somebody checks the drawdown schedule against the loan agreement, somebody else releases the instruction, and they are never the same person. So tell me who does the checking inside your one day.
plain: Stop at SC1. It says five working days must become one. Those five days are not wasted. One person checks the drawdown schedule against the loan agreement. A different person releases the payment instruction. They are never the same person. So tell me who does that checking inside your single day.

natural: I do not know yet.
plain: I do not know the answer yet.

natural: It goes on the sheet as an assumption to be tested. Not as an argument I intend to win this morning.
plain: I will write it down as an assumption that we must test. I will not treat it as an argument to win today.

natural: Three boxes. Steering Committee, Business Implementation Group, Core Team. Everyone here is in one of them and I will tell you which before lunch.
plain: There are three groups: the Project Steering Committee, the Business Implementation Group and the Project Core Team. Everyone in this room belongs to one of them, and I will say which one before lunch.

natural: On approach. We buy this platform. We do not build it.
plain: About the approach. We will buy this platform. We will not build it ourselves.

natural: You have said that four times since March.
plain: You have said that four times since March.

natural: And I will say it in September, when somebody in my own division proposes we build it. Minute it, Henry.
plain: And I will say it again in September, when somebody from my own division suggests we build it. Henry, please record it in the minutes.

natural: Before the plans. The collateral register report — the two pages of lessons learned. One page is about business experts promised part-time.
plain: One thing before we discuss the plans. There is a report from the collateral register project, with two pages of lessons learned. One whole page is about business experts who were promised part-time.

natural: Which is why item eight is the list of plans this project actually needs. Whatever we settle on lands in the Handbook, and the Handbook is the thing you will be held to.
plain: That is why item eight on the agenda is the list of plans this project really needs. Whatever we agree goes into the Project Handbook, and the Handbook is the document that will hold you to it.

natural: Then I want my half hour on the quarterly interest notices. Four hundred letters a quarter, merged in Word, checked twice, posted by a human being. Worst job in the division, and it reads the same loan data CASTOR will hold.
plain: Then I want half an hour on the quarterly interest notices. We send 400 letters every three months. They are merged in Word, checked twice, and posted by a person. It is the worst job in the division, and it uses the same loan data that CASTOR will hold.

natural: She is right about the letters. I have signed six hundred of them.
plain: She is right about the letters. I have signed six hundred of them myself.

natural: Somebody halfway down the table says it would be mad not to fix them while the platform is open. The room warms to the idea in about forty seconds.
plain: Someone in the middle of the table says it would be foolish not to fix the letters while the platform is being built. Within about forty seconds, the room likes the idea.

natural: Next to eight point four million it costs nothing.
plain: Compared with 8.4 million euro, it would cost nothing.

natural: It is 11:40. Twenty-one faces, and the ceiling tile, turn to you.
plain: It is 11:40. Twenty-one people, and the video picture of the ceiling, are all looking at you.

natural: Written down, not signed off. Marie, if it survives the assessment you get your letters. If it does not, you will know who said no and why.
plain: It is written down, but not approved. Marie, if it passes the assessment, you get your letters. If it does not, you will know who refused and for what reason.

natural: Then put it in writing, because what I took to Lorenzo's board on the twenty-fourth said something else.
plain: Then write it down properly, because the document I took to Lorenzo's board on 24 March said something different.

natural: Understood. That is the last idea I bring into one of these rooms.
plain: I understand. That is the last idea I will bring to a meeting like this.

natural: I could. I would be deciding on a number that nobody in this room has estimated.
plain: I could decide. But I would be deciding about a cost that nobody in this room has estimated.

natural: Friday, twenty past eight. Rain on the glass, a tram sliding past below, and eleven pages of Gantt's handwriting on the table between you.
plain: It is Friday at 08:20. Rain runs down the window and a tram passes below. Eleven pages of Gantt's handwritten notes lie on the table between you.

natural: Eleven pages. I can have a full transcript by Monday.
plain: There are eleven pages. I can produce a complete written record by Monday.

natural: I do not want a transcript.
plain: I do not want a full written record.

natural: Gantt puts the pages down with the flat, careful movement of a man who spent an evening on them.
plain: Gantt puts the pages down slowly and carefully. He clearly spent an evening writing them.

natural: Four things. What was raised. What was identified as a risk. What was decided. What somebody proposed to change. Everything else is texture, and I will read the texture in your notebook if I ever need it.
plain: I need four things. The issues that were raised. The risks that were found. The decisions that were taken. The changes that were proposed. Everything else is background detail, and I can read your notebook if I ever need it.

natural: Then the deputy. Finance and Control. Ilona Vas, on the attendance grid, in full.
plain: Then we must record the deputy. She came from Finance and Control. Her name is Ilona Vas, and it goes on the attendance list in full.

natural: In full. In two years somebody will ask whether Finance and Control were in the room when the same-day reconciliation criterion was explained.
plain: Yes, in full. In two years somebody will ask whether Finance and Control were present when the same-day reconciliation target was explained.

natural: Three risks came out of that room and not one of them is an IT risk. Has anybody noticed that.
plain: Three risks came out of that meeting. None of them is an IT risk. Has anyone noticed that?

natural: Ratification of the Treaty reform is not complete, and we have promised to onboard the backstop in six weeks when it is. The parallel run in early 2028 sits next to an EFSF bond rollover. And Lending Operations cannot release its people for two years without something else giving.
plain: First, the Treaty reform is not yet ratified, and we have promised to add the backstop instrument within six weeks once it is. Second, the parallel run in early 2028 falls close to an EFSF bond rollover. Third, Lending Operations cannot release its staff for two years unless something else is dropped.

natural: Write the third one with names in it. It sounds like weather until it says Marie Curie, forty days.
plain: Write the third risk with names in it. Without names it sounds like bad weather. With them it says Marie Curie, forty days.

natural: Good. All three go in the minutes.
plain: Good. All three risks go into the minutes.

natural: In the minutes and in the logs. The minutes summarise a morning. The Risk, Issue and Decision Logs are the registers, and they have been open since January.
plain: They go in the minutes and in the logs. The minutes are a summary of one morning. The Risk Log, the Issue Log and the Decision Log are the real registers, and they have been open since January.

natural: And the interest notices? There is no Change Log.
plain: And what about the interest notices? We do not have a Change Log.

natural: There is as of this week. Status Submitted, which is where every change starts, and from this morning Marie's letters are an entry with a number rather than an idea somebody had at a whiteboard.
plain: We have one from this week. The status is Submitted, which is the first status of every change. From this morning, Marie's letters are a numbered entry, not just an idea from a whiteboard.

natural: Florence reads the draft standing up, coat still on, on her way to a Board of Directors briefing at nine.
plain: Florence reads the draft while standing, still wearing her coat. She is on her way to a Board of Directors briefing at 09:00.

natural: If I sign this, what have I approved?
plain: If I sign this document, what am I approving?

natural: Nothing. It records what happened.
plain: Nothing. It only records what happened.

natural: What the room agreed the project needs — the list of plans, the tailoring, the escalation rules — becomes the Handbook. That is the one you approve, and I would like it in front of you before the end of the month.
plain: What the room agreed the project needs — the list of plans, the tailoring decisions and the escalation rules — goes into the Project Handbook. That is the document you approve, and I would like you to have it before the end of the month.

natural: Then send it to everyone on the Charter's list, not only the people who turned up. Half my division learns what is happening from documents they were copied into.
plain: Then send the minutes to everyone on the stakeholder list in the Charter, not only to those who attended. Half of my division finds out what is happening from documents they were copied into.

natural: That is eighty-one addresses.
plain: That is eighty-one email addresses.

natural: Eighty-one.
plain: Yes. Eighty-one.

natural: She is gone before the door finishes closing. Gantt is already deleting the transcript he wrote on Thursday evening, page by page, without comment.
plain: She leaves before the door has closed. Gantt is already deleting the full record he wrote on Thursday evening, page by page, and says nothing about it.

natural: Six actions, six owners, six dates. Four of them are yours.
plain: There are six actions, six owners and six due dates. Four of the actions belong to you.

natural: Five. I have just taken the eighty-one addresses.
plain: Five actions. I have just accepted the job of sending it to eighty-one people.

natural: The Minutes of Meeting go out at 16:40, one working day after the meeting. Nobody replies until Tuesday, and the reply is from Legal, who could not see the screen.
plain: The minutes are sent at 16:40, one working day after the meeting. Nobody replies until Tuesday. The only reply is from Legal, who could not see the screen during the meeting.

natural: Forty-one pages, printed, because Florence does not read long documents on a screen. There is a sandwich on her desk that she has not opened since half past twelve.
plain: The draft Project Handbook is 41 pages, printed, because Florence will not read long documents on a screen. A sandwich has been on her desk since 12:30 and she has not opened it.

natural: Forty-one pages of what?
plain: Forty-one pages about what?

natural: How we run this. Not what we build.
plain: How we will run this project. Not what we will build.

natural: Approach, the controlling processes, the rules, the escalation route, and who holds which role. The what is the Charter, and then the Work Plan in June.
plain: It covers the approach, the control processes, the project rules, the escalation route, and who holds which role. What we build is in the Charter, and later in the Work Plan in June.

natural: Give me the one page I would read if I read one.
plain: Tell me the single page I should read, if I only read one.

natural: Two point two. Three critical success factors. Lending Operations releases its people for the whole build. You are visibly the owner of this. SC1 to SC5 are still measurable in 2028.
plain: Section 2.2. It lists three critical success factors. First, Lending Operations releases its staff for the whole build. Second, you are visibly the owner of the project. Third, the five success criteria can still be measured in 2028.

natural: The first one is a promise about my staffing plan, not about your project.
plain: The first one is a promise about my staffing plan. It is not about your project.

natural: Which is why it is up there and not in a wish list at the back.
plain: That is exactly why it is at the front of the document and not in a list of hopes at the back.

natural: Leonardo has been drawing on his copy since he sat down. He turns it round. The project lifecycle, redrawn, with the four phases as nested arcs and the gates as narrow points between them.
plain: Since sitting down, Leonardo has been drawing on his copy. He turns it round to show it. He has redrawn the project lifecycle, with the four phases as curved shapes and the gates as narrow points between them.

natural: Yours is a row of boxes. A gate is not a box, it is a narrowing.
plain: Your version is a row of boxes. But a gate is not a box. It is a narrow point.

natural: It is a beautiful drawing and it is not going in the Handbook.
plain: It is a beautiful drawing, and it will not go into the Handbook.

natural: No. Probably not. Three point two, then. Explain the tailoring table, because I count six management plans and four documents.
plain: No. Probably not. Then let us look at section 3.2. Explain the tailoring table. I count six management plans, but only four documents.

natural: Requirements, issue, quality and communications each get their own document. Risk and change stay as sections 4.1 and 4.4, because a section is enough for them here and a separate plan would only be read by me.
plain: The requirements, issue, quality and communications plans each get their own document. The risk and change plans stay as sections 4.1 and 4.4 of the Handbook. A section is enough for them on this project, and a separate document would only be read by me.

natural: That is a shortcut.
plain: That is a shortcut.

natural: It is a decision, written where you can argue with it. You are arguing with it now, which is the point.
plain: It is a decision, and it is written down where you can challenge it. You are challenging it right now, which is exactly the purpose.

natural: Read three point five out. I want them to hear it before it matters rather than after.
plain: Please read section 3.5 aloud. I want everyone to hear it before it becomes important, not afterwards.

natural: Very low and low, the Core Team decides. Medium, Grace and I decide at the status meeting. High and very high go to the Steering Committee. And it lives here once. Every plan points at it instead of copying it.
plain: Very low and low impact: the Core Team decides. Medium impact: Grace and I decide at the status meeting. High and very high impact: the Steering Committee decides. The procedure is written here once. Every other plan refers to it instead of repeating it.

natural: Six point two. You have deleted the agile roles and you have not appointed an assistant.
plain: Section 6.2. You have removed the agile roles and you have not appointed an assistant project manager.

natural: Both deviations, both written down with a reason next to them. Einstein sits on the Steering Committee on request rather than as a member, and that is written down too.
plain: Both are deviations from the standard roles, and both are written down with a reason. Albert Einstein attends the Steering Committee when invited, rather than as a full member, and that is written down as well.

natural: I cannot configure a platform I have never seen. Nobody in this building has seen it.
plain: I cannot configure a platform that I have never seen. Nobody in this building has seen it.

natural: No. So there is a Training Plan annexed. One line of it is yours: platform configuration, intermediate to advanced, coached by the contractor, finished before Release 1 in March 2027.
plain: That is true. So a Training Plan is attached to the Handbook. One line of it is for you: platform configuration, intermediate to advanced level, taught by the contractor, completed before Release 1 in March 2027.

natural: And four point eleven says how they leave. Contractor staff released when the parallel run ends on the thirtieth of April 2028.
plain: And section 4.11 says how people leave the project. The contractor's staff are released when the parallel run ends on 30 April 2028.

natural: It is a decent book. Who signs it?
plain: It is a good document. Who signs it?

natural: Gantt has the blank PM² template open on his laptop, at section two point two, and he has been sitting on it for ten minutes. The guidance text reads: approved by the Project Steering Committee, as part of the overall Project Handbook approval.
plain: Gantt has the empty PM2 template open on his laptop at section 2.2. He has been waiting ten minutes to mention it. The guidance text there says the objectives are approved by the Project Steering Committee, as part of the overall approval of the Project Handbook.

natural: There. The committee. The Charter went to the committee and this is bigger than the Charter.
plain: There you are. The committee. The Charter went to the committee, and this document is bigger than the Charter.

natural: The printed copy sits between you and Florence, unsigned, with a sandwich next to it that is now four hours old.
plain: The printed copy lies between you and Florence, still unsigned. Beside it is a sandwich that is now four hours old.

natural: Then I will read forty-one pages properly, sitting down, and you will get them back on Monday with things crossed out.
plain: Then I will read all 41 pages properly, sitting down. You will get them back on Monday with parts crossed out.

natural: Good. Then it is the committee's book, not Florence's, and between meetings nobody owns a word of it.
plain: Fine. Then it belongs to the committee and not to Florence. Between meetings, nobody owns any of it.

natural: He will send it back with one line asking why he is reading it, and he will remember that you sent it.
plain: He will return it with one sentence asking why he is reading it. And he will remember that you sent it to him.

natural: I would sign it happily. That is the problem. Then it is an IT document, and Lending Operations will read it as one.
plain: I would happily sign it. That is the problem. It would then be an IT document, and Lending Operations would treat it as one.

natural: The open floor by the window, because every meeting room on this side of the building is taken until noon. Marie Curie is at her desk about eight metres away, on the phone to a paying agent.
plain: You meet on the open floor by the window, because every meeting room on this side of the building is booked until midday. Marie Curie is at her desk about eight metres away, on the phone to a paying agent.

natural: Twenty-two rows. Teams, roles, support, operational, and one group at the bottom for anything domain-specific.
plain: There are twenty-two rows. They are grouped as teams, roles, support, operational roles, and one group at the bottom for anything specific to this kind of project.

natural: Row nineteen has no name in it.
plain: Row nineteen has no name in it.

natural: Contractor's Project Manager. Levallois Systems is not awarded until September, so the row exists and the name does not. If I delete the row I will forget the role.
plain: That row is for the contractor's project manager. The contract with Levallois Systems is not awarded until September, so the row exists but the name does not. If I delete the row, I will forget the role.

natural: Show me sheet two.
plain: Show me the second sheet.

natural: Sheet two is the Key Stakeholder Data Sheet. Mobile number, private email, preferred channel, and a free-text box headed Concerns and needs. It is on the shared drive, which is how Brandeis found it before anyone thought to show him.
plain: Sheet two is the Key Stakeholder Data Sheet. It holds mobile numbers, private email addresses, preferred contact channel, and a free-text box titled Concerns and needs. It sits on the shared drive, which is how Brandeis found it before anyone thought to show it to him.

natural: That box is an opinion about a colleague, held in a project folder, for twenty-six months, on a drive four divisions can open. Purpose, access, retention. In that order.
plain: That box holds an opinion about a colleague. It stays in a project folder for twenty-six months, on a drive that four divisions can open. Tell me the purpose, then who can open it, then when it is deleted. In that order.

natural: Purpose is running the project. Access restricted to the Managing Layer. Retention ends at administrative closure, the twenty-eighth of July 2028.
plain: The purpose is to run the project. Access is limited to the Managing Layer. The retention period ends at administrative closure, on 28 July 2028.

natural: And nothing goes in that box that I would not read aloud to the person it is about.
plain: And I will write nothing in that box that I would not read out loud to the person it describes.

natural: Then move it off the shared drive this morning and it is defensible. The matrix itself was never the problem.
plain: Then move it off the shared drive this morning, and it can be defended. The main matrix was never the problem.

natural: Now do the columns you have been avoiding.
plain: Now let us do the columns you have been avoiding.

natural: Power, interest, influence. Interest is how much they care. Influence is what happens when they say no.
plain: They are power, interest and influence. Interest is how much a person cares about the project. Influence is what happens when that person says no.

natural: Marie. High interest, negative.
plain: Take Marie. High interest, and negative influence.
