plain: The responsibility row says: Accountable, the Project Owner. Responsible, the Business Manager. Supporting, the Project Manager. Informed: the governance body, the Steering Committee, the Solution Provider and the Core Team. Consulted: the Business Implementation Group.

natural: The Steering Committee is only informed.
plain: So the Steering Committee is only informed.

natural: It does not approve this one. You do.
plain: The Steering Committee does not approve this plan. You do.

natural: Then I have been informed.
plain: Then I have now been informed.

natural: By me. Twenty seconds ago.
plain: By me. Twenty seconds ago.

natural: The training design, the cohorts, the communication, who is angry and why — that is Grace's document and it has to be. What I can do is take every activity out of it and put it in the Work Plan with effort, dates and a name.
plain: The design of the training, the groups of learners, the communication, who is unhappy and why: that is Grace's document, and it must be. What I can do is take every activity from it and put it into the Project Work Plan, with effort, dates and a responsible person.

natural: And the money for the trainers?
plain: And who pays for the trainers?

natural: In the Work Plan, under your activities, with your name on the line. Which is the only place you can defend it from.
plain: It goes into the Work Plan, under your activities, with your name on that line. That is the only place from which you can defend it.

natural: Then say that in front of her, not to me.
plain: Then say that in front of Florence, not to me.

natural: Which is the moment. Grace cannot write it this month. You can write it this weekend and you are not allowed to. Florence is standing in the door with her coat over her arm.
plain: This is the decisive moment. Grace cannot write the plan this month. You could write it this weekend, but you are not allowed to. Florence is standing in the doorway with her coat over her arm.

natural: Then I take her off the Board note and write it myself on Sunday. And you will explain to Lorenzo why my paper is thin. That is what asking me costs.
plain: Then I will take her off the Board note and write it myself on Sunday. And you will explain to Lorenzo why my paper is short. That is the price of asking me.

natural: And in January 2028 somebody asks why the plan thinks two of my people will be fine about losing the only part of the job they are known for. You would have had to guess. I would not.
plain: And in January 2028 somebody will ask why the plan assumes two of my staff will be happy to lose the only part of the job they are known for. You would have had to guess. I would not.

natural: Then training becomes something that happens before a date, instead of something that happens to forty people. You will tick it in April 2028 and half of them will still be printing the old procedure.
plain: Then the training becomes something that must happen before a date, instead of something that happens to forty people. You will tick the box in April 2028, and half of them will still be printing the old procedure.

natural: The Planning gate asks whether the business-side activities are planned and resourced. If the answer is not yet, then that is the answer you take into the room, and I will minute it.
plain: The Planning gate asks whether the business-side activities are planned and resourced. If the answer is not yet, then that is the answer you bring to the meeting, and I will write it in the minutes.

natural: Nine in the morning on the sixth floor. Forty desks, twenty-two of them occupied. Grace's plan is printed and lying on the table by the window where people leave biscuits and nobody holds meetings.
plain: It is 09:00 on the sixth floor. There are forty desks and twenty-two people at them. Grace's plan is printed and lying on the table by the window, where people leave biscuits and nobody usually holds meetings.

natural: Section three. Impact on people. Read it out.
plain: Section three, the impact on people. Read it aloud.

natural: Forty loan administrators stop re-keying approximately fourteen hundred payment fields a quarter. Two posts refocus on exception handling and control testing.
plain: Forty loan administrators stop typing about 1,400 payment fields again every three months. Two posts change focus to exception handling and control testing.

natural: Refocus.
plain: Refocus.

natural: Say it better and I will change the sentence.
plain: Say it in a better way and I will change the sentence.

natural: Say what happens to the second pair of eyes.
plain: Say what happens to the second pair of eyes.

natural: It stops being a person reading and becomes the system refusing.
plain: The check stops being one person reading another person's work. It becomes the system refusing to continue.

natural: Then it is a control that has to be tested, not a feature that gets demonstrated. Somebody attempts the forbidden thing every quarter and the report says it failed.
plain: Then it is a control that must be tested, not a feature that is demonstrated. Every three months somebody tries to do the forbidden action, and the report shows that the system stopped them.

natural: Section four is culture. Two paragraphs, and I nearly cut it. Sources of resistance. The two people who built the 2019 workaround are the two people everyone else asks. If they are against this in January 2028, it does not matter what the platform can do.
plain: Section four is about culture. It is two paragraphs long and I almost deleted it. It says where resistance will come from. The two people who built the 2019 workaround are the two people everyone else goes to for help. If they are against the change in January 2028, then it does not matter what the platform can do.

natural: And the training?
plain: And the training?

natural: Three days classroom, then shadowing. Forty people in cohorts, January to April 2028. The Business Implementation Group delivers it. Sixty person-days of trainer time and two rooms I have to book eighteen months out.
plain: Three days in a classroom, then working beside an experienced colleague. Forty people, in small groups, from January to April 2028. The Business Implementation Group delivers the training. It needs sixty person-days of trainer time and two rooms that I must book eighteen months in advance.

natural: Approved.
plain: Approved.

natural: In writing.
plain: In writing, please.

natural: In writing.
plain: In writing.

natural: And it is three lists, not one. What the project does. What Lending Operations does afterwards. What happens after the project has closed.
plain: And there are three lists, not one. What the project itself does. What Lending Operations does afterwards. And what happens after the project has closed.

natural: Annual refresher and a control self-assessment from 2029. Not the project's. Yours.
plain: There will be yearly refresher training and a control self-assessment from 2029. Those are not the project's work. They are yours.

natural: And the backstop, if the Treaty reform ever finishes ratifying. Six weeks from entry into force to a live instrument. Written as a recommendation, not as a commitment.
plain: And the common backstop, if all member states finally approve the Treaty reform. Six weeks from the reform entering into force to a working lending product. It is written as a recommendation, not as a promise.

natural: When do I see the numbers?
plain: When do I see the results?

natural: SC1 to SC5, measured quarterly by Lending Operations, from the first quarter of 2029.
plain: Success criteria SC1 to SC5 are measured every three months by Lending Operations, starting in the first quarter of 2029.

natural: The project ends in July 2028.
plain: The project ends in July 2028.

natural: Yes.
plain: Yes.

natural: She looks down the room at the twenty-two occupied desks for longer than the sentence needs.
plain: Florence looks down the room at the twenty-two occupied desks. She looks for longer than the sentence needed.

natural: So the project ends before it can prove anything.
plain: So the project ends before it can prove that it worked.

natural: Most of them do. That is why the metrics have an owner who is not the project, and why this checklist still has open lines the day you close.
plain: Most projects do. That is why the measurements have an owner outside the project, and why this checklist still has open items on the day the project closes.

natural: Every activity in here is in the Work Plan by Friday, with effort and dates against Grace's name.
plain: Every activity in this plan will be in the Project Work Plan by Friday, with effort and dates, under Grace's name.

natural: Florence signs it there, on the biscuit table, with a pen borrowed from a desk. No committee. No quorum. The Steering Committee will be informed on the twenty-sixth.
plain: Florence signs the plan there, on the biscuit table, using a pen borrowed from a desk. There is no committee and no quorum. The Steering Committee will be informed on 26 June.

natural: On the twenty-sixth of June at eighteen forty, with the building nearly empty, the Project Handbook and the Project Work Plan were baselined. Seven days later the same people sit down on the seventh floor with the plateau green and glaring behind the glass.
plain: On 26 June at 18:40, when the building was almost empty, the Project Handbook and the Project Work Plan were baselined. Seven days later the same people meet on the seventh floor. Behind the glass, the plateau is green and bright.

natural: Item one. Ready for Executing. Go.
plain: Item one on the agenda. Ready for Executing. Please begin.

natural: Planning sheet of the Phase Exit Review Checklist. Forty-three checks. Compliance ninety-eight per cent. Status zero point nine.
plain: This is the Planning sheet of the Phase Exit Review Checklist. It has 43 questions. The compliance score is 98 per cent. The status value is 0.9.

natural: Which means what, exactly?
plain: And what exactly does that mean?

natural: That we are above eighty per cent on the template's own scale. It does not mean anything else.
plain: It means we are above 80 per cent on the scale that the template itself uses. It means nothing more than that.

natural: I assured the answers. Two of them are not Yes.
plain: I checked the answers as quality assurance. Two of them are not Yes.

plain: Say which two.

Yes, partially, with the award date in the comment. And test resourcing in the second half of 2027, where I have two profiles named and one that is still only a profile.
plain: First, the Outsourcing Plan check. The Corporate Investment Board approved the plan on 24 June, but there is no tender yet and no supplier. So the answer is Yes, partially, with the award date written in the comment. Second, the staffing of testing in the second half of 2027. Two roles have names against them and one is still only a role.

natural: For completeness. All four project-specific plans exist and all four are approved.
plain: For the record: all four project-specific plans exist, and all four are approved.

natural: Approved by four different people, which took me until last week to get straight in my head.
plain: Approved by four different people. It took me until last week to understand that properly.

natural: The Corporate Investment Board for outsourcing. This committee for deliverables acceptance. This committee again for transition. The Project Owner, on her own, for business implementation.
plain: The Corporate Investment Board approves the Outsourcing Plan. This committee approves the Deliverables Acceptance Plan. This committee also approves the Transition Plan. The Project Owner approves the Business Implementation Plan by herself.

natural: And the Project Manager for none of them.
plain: And the Project Manager approves none of them.

natural: The Project Manager for writing three and supporting the fourth. Accountability was never mine to hold.
plain: The Project Manager writes three of them and supports the fourth. The accountability was never mine to hold.

natural: Architecture Office. One observation, and then I will stop. The payment gateway interface is planned against a target architecture that is itself under review this autumn.
plain: Speaking for the Architecture Office. One comment, and then I will stop. The interface to the payment gateway is designed against a target architecture, and that architecture will itself be reviewed this autumn.

natural: Logged as a dependency, not a deviation. If the target architecture moves, it reaches us as a Change Request under the Project Change Management Plan, not as a surprise in a status report.
plain: It is recorded as a dependency, not as a deviation. If the target architecture changes, it comes to us as a formal Change Request under the Project Change Management Plan. It does not arrive as a surprise inside a status report.

natural: Then I have nothing to object to.
plain: Then I have no objection.

natural: My question is narrower than everybody else's.
plain: My question is narrower than everyone else's.

natural: Are there major deviations from the approved Business Case or the Project Charter?
plain: Are there any major differences from the approved Business Case or the Project Charter?

natural: No. Eight point four million, unchanged. Three thousand one hundred person-days, unchanged. Twenty-six months, unchanged. SC1 to SC5 unchanged, and each of them now behind a named acceptance criterion.
plain: No. The budget is still 8.4 million euro. The effort is still 3,100 person-days. The duration is still 26 months. Success criteria SC1 to SC5 are unchanged, and each one now has a named acceptance criterion behind it.

natural: Then this gate is not mine. Enjoy it. They mostly are.
plain: Then this gate is not mine to decide. Enjoy that. Most of them are mine.

natural: One question. Nothing in those forty-three checks asks whether the thing will work.
plain: One question. None of those 43 checks asks whether the system will actually work.

natural: No. The gate asks whether Planning did its job. Whether it works is what the next two years are for, and you are the person who tells us.
plain: No. The gate asks whether the Planning Phase did its job. Whether the system works is the question for the next two years, and you are the person who will tell us.

natural: Ninety-eight per cent. I take it that means we are through.
plain: Ninety-eight per cent. I assume that means we can move on.

natural: Gantt's pen has stopped. Deming is looking at the table. Nobody in the room is going to answer that for you.
plain: Gantt has stopped writing. Deming is looking at the table. Nobody in this room is going to answer that question for you.

natural: Then ask properly and I will put it to the room. Kick-off the tenth of July. Henry, minute the two partial answers with the sentences he used, not with the number.
plain: Then ask properly and I will put it to the committee. The Executing Kick-off Meeting is on 10 July. Henry, record the two partial answers in the minutes using his words, not the score.

natural: The band is a status colour. It has no authority over anything. If ninety-eight passes on its own, then so does a hundred per cent of forty-three questions nobody asked properly.
plain: The band is only a status colour. It has no authority. If 98 per cent were enough by itself, then so would be 100 per cent on 43 questions that nobody answered honestly.

natural: You would be sending me a partial answer about a tender I already approved the method for. Send me deviations. Do not send me your homework.
plain: You would be sending me a partial answer about a tender whose method I have already approved. Send me deviations. Do not send me your homework.

natural: Then in 2028 the record shows a Project Manager who moved his own project to Executing. I would rather write down that eight people did it in nine minutes.
plain: Then in 2028 the record will show a Project Manager who moved his own project into the Executing Phase. I would rather write that eight people decided it together in nine minutes.

natural: The plateau is in its third week of heat and Schuman is the only room on this floor whose air conditioning works, which is most of why nineteen people are in it. Gantt has laid a printed agenda on every chair. Nobody has picked one up.
plain: Luxembourg is in its third week of hot weather. Schuman is the only room on this floor with working air conditioning. That is one reason nineteen people are here. Gantt put a printed agenda on every chair. Nobody has taken one.

natural: Ninety minutes. I will chair.
plain: You have ninety minutes. I will lead the meeting.

natural: The agenda went out on the third with the Handbook and the Work Plan. Nobody commented. I run it. You do the two minutes at the end that only you can do.
plain: I sent the agenda on 3 July, with the Project Handbook and the Project Work Plan. Nobody sent comments. I will lead the meeting. At the end you speak for two minutes, because only you can say that part.

natural: Which two minutes?
plain: Which two minutes do you mean?

natural: The ones where the Project Owner says out loud, to forty people, that the fifteenth of May 2028 is not a target.
plain: The part where the Project Owner tells forty people that 15 May 2028 is not just a target. It is the date.

natural: She sits. Gantt opens a laptop and then a paper notebook, in that order.
plain: Nightingale sits down. Gantt opens a laptop, and then a paper notebook.

natural: Minutes. Out within two working days. Anything raised as a risk, an issue, a decision or a change goes into the log as well, not only into the minutes.
plain: I will write the minutes. They go out within two working days. Any risk, issue, decision or change raised here also goes into the correct project log, not only into the minutes.

natural: Who is the empty row for?
plain: Who are the empty seats at the back for?

natural: The vendor.
plain: For the company that will build the system.

natural: There is no vendor. There are three bids and an evaluation panel that first meets on the ninth of September.
plain: There is no vendor yet. Three companies have sent offers. The panel that evaluates them meets for the first time on 9 September.

natural: Item one. Handbook and Work Plan at the level this room can use and no deeper. Seven work packages. Three thousand one hundred person-days. Eight point four million. Release one, twenty-sixth of March 2027. Release two, the seventeenth of December. Parallel run from January 2028. Go-live the fifteenth of May.
plain: Item one. I present the Project Handbook and the Project Work Plan at the level of detail this room needs, and no more. Seven work packages. 3,100 person-days. 8.4 million euro. Release 1 on 26 March 2027. Release 2 on 17 December 2027. Parallel run from January 2028. Go-live on 15 May 2028.

natural: Then a question that is not on your agenda. When an architect tells me a screen cannot be built the way loan administration actually works, who wins?
plain: Now a question that is not on your agenda. An architect tells me a screen cannot work the way my team really works. Who decides?

natural: It is item four and you have opened it early. We agree the conflict resolution process this morning, all of us. Then I present the escalation procedure, which is not open, because Florence signed it in June.
plain: That is item four. You have started it early. This morning we all agree the process for settling disagreements. Then I present the escalation procedure. That one is not open for discussion, because Florence approved it in June.

natural: Agree. Meaning a vote?
plain: You say agree. Do you mean we vote on it?

natural: Meaning we settle now that a disagreement is worked where it arises, in writing, for five working days, with Grace and me copied. On the sixth day it goes up. Where up goes is section three point five and you have all had it since June.
plain: I mean we agree now that a disagreement is worked on at the level where it starts, in writing, for five working days, with Grace and me in copy. On the sixth day it is escalated. The route upwards is in Handbook section 3.5, which you have all had since June.

natural: Five days. Some of us can fall out considerably faster than that.
plain: Five days is generous. Some of us can start an argument much faster than that.

natural: Item six will say that I am independent of the Project Manager. Say it in July. By September nobody remembers reading it.
plain: Item six will state that I work independently of the Project Manager. Say that clearly in July. By September, nobody remembers reading it.

natural: Items five and six, then. Stakeholder Matrix. Risk, issue and change management. Quality assurance and control, and who does which.
plain: So, items five and six. The Project Stakeholder Matrix. Then the risk, issue and change management processes. Then the quality assurance and quality control activities, and who performs each of them.

natural: And item seven is where I get to say what I need from you.
plain: And item seven is where I say what I need from you.

natural: Item seven is where I say what I expect of the Core Team. I will take yours in the same twenty minutes and I would rather have it in the room than in a corridor in November.
plain: Item seven is where I explain what I expect from the Project Core Team. I will also listen to what you expect from me, in the same twenty minutes. I would rather hear it here than in a corridor in November.

natural: Ground rules are item eight and I have brought a flipchart, because a thing written on a flipchart gets argued with and a thing on a slide does not.
plain: Ground rules are item eight. I brought a flipchart. People argue with something written on a flipchart. They do not argue with a slide.

natural: First rule. Nothing is real until it is in a log. A risk in the corridor is a conversation. A risk in the Risk Log has an owner, a score and a strategy.
plain: First ground rule. Nothing is real until it is written in a log. A risk mentioned in the corridor is only a conversation. A risk in the Risk Log has an owner, a score and a response strategy.

natural: Second. If it has a screen my people touch, my people see it before anyone says it is done.
plain: Second rule. If it has a screen that my staff use, my staff must see it before anyone calls it finished.

natural: Third. Nobody books my two business experts without asking me first. They have a quarter-end and it does not move for anyone in this room.
plain: Third rule. Nobody books my two business experts without asking me first. They have quarter-end work, and that work moves for nobody here.

natural: Nightingale has not looked at the flipchart once. She is looking at the row of empty chairs at the back of the room.
plain: Nightingale has not looked at the flipchart at all. She is looking at the empty row of chairs at the back.

natural: Levallois will win this tender. Everyone in this room knows it. Should they be sitting in it?
plain: Levallois Systems will probably win this tender. Everyone here knows that. Should they be in the room today?

natural: Then say it at item seven, out loud, so that nobody in September thinks I forgot to invite them.
plain: Then say that clearly at item seven. In September I do not want anyone to think I forgot to invite them.

natural: Three bids. One of them sitting in our risk register. I would quite like to still have a division in October.
plain: There are three bidders. You would seat one of them in front of our risk register. I would prefer to still have a division in October.

natural: Then who is left to answer for the eight items, and who do I chase when item three is not presented?
plain: Then who answers for the eight agenda items, and who do I contact when item three is not presented?

natural: Then when the architect and I disagree in November, we will invent a process in November. Badly, and in front of a deadline.
plain: Then when the architect and I disagree in November, we will invent a process in November. We will do it badly, and under time pressure.

natural: The Project Support Office is two desks, four filing cabinets and a window facing the car park. Gantt has printed the Work Plan across six sheets of A3 and taped them to the wall in the wrong order, then fixed it.
plain: The Project Support Office has two desks, four filing cabinets and a window that looks at the car park. Gantt printed the Project Work Plan on six large sheets and taped them to the wall. He put them up in the wrong order and then corrected it.

natural: That is the baseline. Twenty-sixth of June, version one point zero, approved. One copy. It does not move.
plain: That is the baseline. Approved on 26 June, version 1.0. There is one copy and it does not change.

natural: And the copy on my drive?
plain: What about the copy on my own drive?

natural: Is a photograph of it.
plain: That is only a picture of it. It is not the baseline.

natural: There is nothing to measure yet. Two weeks in, no contract, no build. That is exactly why we are doing this today.
plain: There is nothing to measure yet. We are two weeks into the phase, with no contract and no build work. That is exactly why we are doing this today.

natural: You have called a meeting about measuring nothing.
plain: So you have called a meeting about measuring nothing.

natural: I have called a meeting about what the word done will mean in March. Agreed in July it is a definition. Agreed in March it is an argument with a release in it.
plain: I have called a meeting about what the word done will mean in March. If we agree it in July, it is a definition. If we agree it in March, it is an argument, and there is a release waiting behind it.

natural: Florence knows we are doing this?
plain: Does Florence know that we are doing this?

natural: It is her name in the accountable column. My job is to hand her something she can read on a Tuesday without a translator. She sees the shape of it next week.
plain: Florence is Accountable for monitoring. My job is to give her something she can read on a Tuesday without help. She will see the format next week.

natural: Then ban percentages. Ninety per cent complete means a developer feels good on a Thursday. It has never once meant that nine tenths of the work is behind us.
plain: Then do not allow percentages. Ninety per cent complete means a developer felt good on a Thursday. It has never meant that nine tenths of the work is finished.

natural: So a task is at zero or at a hundred, and it reaches a hundred when somebody who did not build it says so.
plain: So a task is either at zero or at one hundred. It reaches one hundred only when somebody who did not build it confirms it.

natural: Verified by whom, in July, before there is anything to verify?
plain: Verified by whom? It is July, and there is nothing yet to verify.

natural: Named now, task by task, in the plan. Ada for specifications. Marie's people for anything with a screen. Grace for anything that touches a payment instruction.
plain: We name the verifier now, task by task, in the Project Work Plan. Ada for specifications. Marie Curie's staff for anything with a screen. Grace for anything that touches a payment instruction.

natural: Then I want four things every second Tuesday, in the same shape every time. Critical path tasks and the ones about to become critical. Deliverables finished and verified. Days burned against days planned. And the four logs.
plain: Then I want four things every second Tuesday, always in the same format. First, the critical path tasks and the tasks about to become critical. Second, deliverables that are finished and verified. Third, days used compared with days planned. Fourth, the four project logs.

natural: That is four. What about people?
plain: That is four things. What about the people?

natural: People is not a number.
plain: People cannot be turned into a number.

natural: People is the first thing that goes wrong and the last thing anybody writes down. Ask me in February how the test team is and I will tell you before any of your columns do.
plain: People are the first thing that goes wrong and the last thing anybody writes down. Ask me in February how the test team is feeling. I will know before any of your columns show it.

natural: Then it is the fifth thing and I collect it by walking around, not on a form. Half of what I will need never arrives at a scheduled meeting.
plain: Then people is the fifth thing. I will collect it by walking around and talking, not with a form. Half of what I need will never come to me in a planned meeting.

natural: Second Tuesday. My architects are already in two stand-ups and a sprint review, and they will be in a contractor's ceremony as well by October.
plain: Every second Tuesday. My architects already attend two short daily meetings and a sprint review. By October they will also attend the contractor's own meetings.

natural: They report once. Gantt takes the sprint data and reshapes it. Nobody on CASTOR types the same number into two systems.
plain: They will report once. Gantt takes the sprint data and puts it into our format. On Project CASTOR, nobody types the same number into two different systems.

natural: I want that in writing.
plain: I want that written down.

natural: Handbook, section five. In writing since June, read by nobody, which is the other reason we are all here.
plain: It is in the Project Handbook, section 5. It has been written down since June and nobody read it. That is the other reason we are meeting today.

natural: And when the number is bad?
plain: And what happens when the number is bad?

natural: Then it is bad on the same Tuesday as everything else. Monitoring decides nothing. It only makes sure that when we do decide, we are deciding about the project and not about a mood.
plain: Then it is reported as bad on the same Tuesday as everything else. Monitoring does not decide anything. It only makes sure that when we do decide, we decide about the real project and not about how people feel.

natural: Leonardo studies the six sheets for a while. Then he takes a pencil out of his jacket and, without asking anybody, draws a short line down the margin of sheet four.
plain: Leonardo looks at the six sheets for a while. Then he takes a pencil from his jacket and draws a short line in the margin of sheet four, without asking permission.

natural: Data migration. Four hundred and eighty person-days, one owner, no verifier. Put a name there before you measure anything at all.
plain: Look at data migration. It has 480 person-days and one owner, but no verifier. Write a name there before you measure anything.

natural: Gustave Eiffel has been in the building for forty minutes and has already asked where the goods lift is. The contract was signed a week ago. He takes the chair with a view of the door and keeps his coat on.
plain: Gustave Eiffel has been in the building for forty minutes. He has already asked where the goods lift is. The contract was signed one week ago. He sits where he can see the door and keeps his coat on.

natural: Before anything else. Who may speak to my engineers?
plain: First question, before anything else. Who is allowed to talk to my engineers?

natural: Me, through you. Everyone else, through me, through you.
plain: I speak to them through you. Everyone else speaks to me, and then I speak to you.

natural: Then we shall get along. My status report reaches you by the fifth of each month. If it is late, it is late because I am late, not because someone in your building is thinking about it.
plain: Then we will work well together. My contractor status report will reach you by the fifth day of each month. If it is late, that is my fault, not the fault of anyone in your building.

natural: Gantt puts one sheet in the middle of the table. Ten rows, three columns, a figure at the bottom.
plain: Gantt puts a single sheet of paper in the middle of the table. It has ten rows, three columns and a figure at the bottom.

natural: Stakeholders Checklist, planning phase. Ninety per cent. Signed at the gate on the third of July.
plain: This is the Stakeholders Checklist for the Planning Phase. It scores ninety per cent. It was signed at the gate on 3 July.

natural: Ninety is the part I already know. I want the ten.
plain: I already know about the ninety per cent. I am interested in the missing ten per cent.

natural: Row seven. Did you inform the key stakeholders about the change process and the change log. Answer, yes, partially.
plain: Look at row seven. Did you tell the key stakeholders about the change process and the Change Log? The answer is yes, partially.

natural: Partially means the cabinets have not been briefed. Verbal scope requests are still arriving, and they arrive at me.
plain: Partially means the private offices of the Board members have not been briefed. Requests to add scope still arrive by telephone, and they arrive to me.

natural: Arriving how?
plain: How do they arrive?

natural: A call in March asking whether we could just add something. Two more in June.
plain: A telephone call in March asking if we could simply add something. Two more calls in June.

natural: And you said?
plain: And what did you answer?

natural: Yes. In writing. On a form. Two of the three went quiet.
plain: I said yes, in writing, on a Change Request Form. Two of the three requests then stopped.

natural: And the third?
plain: And what about the third one?

natural: The third is why row seven says partially. He is neither for us nor against us and has not decided which, and those are the ones the matrix is worst at.
plain: The third request is why row seven says partially. That person is not clearly for the project or against it, and has not decided. The Project Stakeholder Matrix is worst at describing those people.

natural: Row ten. Reconciliation requirements still open with me. That is not partially. That is not started.
plain: Now row ten. The reconciliation requirements are still open with me. That is not partially done. That is not started.

natural: It is mine and it is late. I will get you three hours before the fifteenth of October.
plain: That is my responsibility and it is late. I will book you three hours before 15 October.

natural: A slot is not an answer. Bring the two-day reconciliation with you and we will find out how much of it is the old loan references.
plain: A meeting slot is not an answer. Bring the current two-day reconciliation process with you. Then we will see how much of the problem comes from the old loan reference numbers.

natural: Row twelve. No. Formal announcement to the user groups, not made. That one is mine and it stays a no until Grace tells me what I am announcing.
plain: Now row twelve. The answer is no. The formal announcement to the user groups has not been made. That is my task. It stays no until Grace tells me what I am announcing.

natural: Forty administrators. I cannot tell them what changes until the Business Implementation Plan says who retrains them and in whose time.
plain: There are forty loan administrators. I cannot tell them what will change until the Business Implementation Plan says who retrains them, and during whose working time.

natural: Then row twelve takes a date, not a no. This is not a school report. It is a list of actions with names and dates on them, and we look at it again at the next gate.
plain: Then row twelve gets a date instead of a no. This checklist is not a school report. It is a list of actions with names and dates. We will look at it again at the next phase gate.

natural: Row thirteen concerns me. Do the stakeholders remain the same for the next phase. It says yes. Then it says contractor roles to be added at contract award.
plain: Row thirteen concerns me. It asks whether the stakeholders stay the same in the next phase. It says yes. Then it says that contractor roles will be added when the contract is awarded.

natural: You are the addition.
plain: You are that addition.

natural: Then your matrix is one week out of date and your distribution list with it. I would prefer my first report to reach the right people the first time.
plain: Then your Project Stakeholder Matrix is one week out of date, and so is your distribution list. I would prefer my first report to reach the right people immediately.

natural: Matrix updated today. Communications plan aligned this week. You get the list before you write a word of it.
plain: I will update the matrix today and align the Communications Management Plan this week. You will get the distribution list before you write anything.

natural: And the checklist gets a version and a date, and the July one stays where it is. Nobody rewrites July in September.
plain: And the checklist gets a version number and a date. The July version stays as it is. Nobody rewrites July in September.

natural: The project area is eleven desks, a coffee machine that grinds its beans very loudly at the worst moments, and one whiteboard that Nikola Tesla has covered edge to edge in a diagram nobody asked him for.
plain: The project area has eleven desks, a coffee machine that is very loud, and one whiteboard. Nikola Tesla has filled the whole whiteboard with a diagram that nobody asked him to draw.

natural: It is a product model. Every instrument this institution has ever had, and four it does not have yet.
plain: It is a product model. It covers every lending instrument the ESM has ever had, and four more that do not exist yet.

natural: Two of which do not exist in law.
plain: Two of those four do not exist in law.

natural: Nikola. The Work Plan has you on the configuration engine, due the ninth of November. Where are you?
plain: Nikola, the Project Work Plan says you are working on the configuration engine, due on 9 November. Where are you with it?

natural: Ahead. Of the wrong plan.
plain: I am ahead of schedule. But it is the wrong schedule.

natural: Eiffel, who has been standing by the window with his coat still on, writes something in a small book.
plain: Eiffel is standing by the window, still wearing his coat. He writes something in a small notebook.

natural: He is booked to my task 4.2 until the sixth. If he is doing something else, I would like to know before I sign the timesheets, not after.
plain: He is assigned to my task 4.2 until 6 November. If he is doing different work, I want to know before I sign the timesheets, not afterwards.

natural: He is doing something else, and that is mine, not his. I let two weeks pass without looking at what was actually being built.
plain: He is doing different work. That is my mistake, not his. I let two weeks pass without checking what was really being built.

natural: The diagram is not wrong.
plain: The diagram itself is not wrong.

natural: It is not wrong. It is not the ninth of November.
plain: It is not wrong. But it is not what is due on 9 November.

natural: To an architect those are the same sentence.
plain: To an architect, those two statements mean the same thing.

natural: They are not the same sentence to me. I cannot write acceptance tests against a model that grows every Friday afternoon.
plain: They do not mean the same thing to me. I cannot write acceptance tests against a model that gets bigger every Friday afternoon.

natural: Then write them against six instruments and rewrite them in eighteen months when the seventh arrives.
plain: Then write the tests for six instruments now, and rewrite them in eighteen months when a seventh instrument arrives.

natural: Yes. That is the job.
plain: Yes. That is exactly the job.

natural: A silence of the particular kind that follows somebody being told something true.
plain: There is a short silence. It is the kind that follows a true statement that nobody can argue with.

natural: Interim check on the fifth. Six instruments configured, loaded into the test environment, Ada runs her pack against them. It passes, the task closes, Gustave signs. It fails, we are having this conversation again on the sixth with less time.
plain: We will do an interim check on 5 November. Six instruments configured and loaded into the test environment. Ada runs her regression pack against them. If it passes, the task is closed and Gustave signs. If it fails, we have this same conversation on 6 November with less time left.

natural: Payment on acceptance. Not on effort. That is the contract and it suits me — my people work better against a date somebody will actually check.
plain: We are paid when work is accepted, not for the effort we spend. That is what the contract says, and I prefer it. My staff work better when a date will really be checked.

natural: And my two?
plain: And what about my two business experts?

natural: Second week of November.
plain: I need them in the second week of November.

natural: Quarter-end is the second week of November.
plain: Quarter-end work happens in the second week of November.

natural: Then the third week, and I need to know today, because the third week is where the migration dry run sits and the dry run needs the production calendar.
plain: Then I take the third week. I need to know today, because the data migration dry run is planned for that week, and the dry run needs the live production calendar.

natural: The production calendar has a Greek repayment on the eleventh. Nobody rehearses anything on the eleventh.
plain: The production calendar has a Greek loan repayment on 11 November. Nobody runs a rehearsal on that day.

natural: Then the seventeenth, and I owe you a workshop invitation that says four days when it means four days.
plain: Then we do it on 17 November. And I owe you a workshop invitation that says four days when it really means four days.

natural: The model will still be right in five years.
plain: My model will still be correct in five years.

natural: It might be. On the ninth of November I need it to be right about six instruments and one value date.
plain: Perhaps it will. But on 9 November I need it to be correct about six instruments and one value date.

natural: Tesla photographs the whiteboard before he wipes half of it off. Eiffel writes one more line in the small book and finally takes off his coat.
plain: Tesla takes a photograph of the whiteboard, then wipes half of it clean. Eiffel writes one more line in his notebook and finally takes off his coat.

natural: Werner has one window and a blind that has hung at an angle since 2019. Deming has brought a printed checklist with ten area names down its left edge, and a pen he does not use on his own copy.
plain: Room Werner has one window and a broken blind that has hung crooked since 2019. Deming has brought a printed checklist. It has ten area names down the left side. He holds a pen, but he does not write on his own copy.

natural: Three questions. They are the same three every time. Is the control there. Is it being used. Does it work. Start with yours, Nikola. Peer review before merge, Quality Management Plan page four, approved in June with everything else.
plain: I have three questions. They are always the same three. Is the control in place? Is it being used? Does it actually work? We start with yours, Nikola. A second developer reviews the code before it is merged. It is in the Quality Management Plan on page four, approved in June with all the other plans.

natural: It happens on every merge.
plain: It happens every single time we merge code.

natural: Show me.
plain: Please show me the proof.

natural: Ask my team.
plain: You can ask my team.

natural: I did. Three said always. One said usually. That is four opinions and no evidence.
plain: I already asked them. Three people said always. One person said usually. That gives me four opinions and no evidence.

natural: Tesla says nothing for four seconds, which for him is a great deal of nothing. Then he opens a laptop and produces, in ninety seconds, an export of two hundred and fourteen merges with a reviewer name against two hundred and nine of them.
plain: Tesla says nothing for four seconds, which is a long silence for him. Then he opens a laptop. In ninety seconds he produces a list of 214 merges. 209 of them have the name of a reviewer next to them.

natural: Five.
plain: Five have no reviewer.

natural: Five out of two hundred and fourteen.
plain: That is five out of two hundred and fourteen.

natural: Five is not a scandal. Five with no reason recorded is a non-conformity. Write the reason against each one and it becomes a note instead.
plain: Five is not a scandal. But five with no recorded reason is a non-conformity. Write the reason next to each one, and it becomes only a note.

natural: This is my area. My division produces the deliverables and I answer for their quality.
plain: This is my area. My division produces the deliverables and I answer for their quality.

natural: For the deliverables. Not for this.
plain: You answer for the deliverables. You do not answer for this activity.

natural: Then say the difference slowly, because I have been signing quality plans for eleven years.
plain: Then explain the difference clearly, because I have been signing quality plans for eleven years.

natural: Quality of the product is yours. Whether this project's own controls exist, are used, and do anything is mine to answer for and theirs to prove. It is the one row in the whole method where my name sits in the accountable column and the Core Team's sits in the responsible one.
plain: The quality of the product is yours. But whether this project's own controls exist, are used, and have any effect is my accountability, and the Project Core Team must provide the proof. This is the only row in the whole method where the Project Manager is Accountable and the Project Core Team is Responsible.

natural: One row.
plain: Only one row.

natural: One.
plain: Only one.

natural: And I set the standard and review the outputs, which is exactly why I do not report to him. An independent reviewer who reports to the person he reviews is a decoration.
plain: And I set the quality standards and review the project's outputs. That is why I do not report to the Project Manager. An independent reviewer who reports to the person he reviews is only decoration.

natural: Do my people produce evidence too? Because if the answer is yes, I need it to be four hours a month, not four days.

natural: Rain comes in sideways off the plateau. The monthly reassessment starts eleven minutes late because the lift is out again and Henry Gantt will not take four floors at speed.
plain: Rain is blowing across the plateau. The monthly risk review starts 11 minutes late. The lift is broken again, and Henry Gantt refuses to hurry up four floors of stairs.

natural: Nine open, three moved since August, and I would like to be out of here by ten. R-03, the backstop is not ratified, three by four. R-05, forty administrators unavailable for retraining, three by three. R-09, the parallel run sits across an EFSF rollover, four by three, and it has said Assessing since June.
plain: There are 9 open risks in the Risk Log. Three have changed since August. I would like to be out of here by 10:00. Risk R-03: the common backstop is not yet ratified, likelihood 3, impact 4. Risk R-05: 40 loan administrators may not be free for retraining, likelihood 3, impact 3. Risk R-09: the parallel run happens at the same time as an EFSF bond rollover, likelihood 4, impact 3, and its status has said Assessing since June.

natural: R-07. Take it to five.
plain: Now take risk R-07. Raise its likelihood score to 5.

natural: On what?
plain: Based on what evidence?

natural: On five. Four means the room can still decide to do nothing about it and feel reasonable.
plain: Raise it to 5 because it should be 5. A score of 4 lets this meeting decide to do nothing and still feel sensible.

natural: That is not what the column is for. Four by five. Twenty, and it has been twenty since the thirty-first of March.
plain: The likelihood column records probability. It is not a tool for pushing people to act. R-07 has likelihood 4 and impact 5. Multiply them: the risk level is 20. It has been 20 since 31 March.

natural: Twenty is red. Red goes to the Committee in the monthly pack and to the Corporate Investment Board on top of that. Sixteen is where that starts and we are four above it.
plain: A risk level of 20 is red. Red risks go to the Project Steering Committee in the monthly report, and also to the Corporate Investment Board. The threshold for that is 16, and this risk is 4 points above it.

natural: Writing twenty in a spreadsheet does not change what a man decides about his own career.
plain: Writing the number 20 in a spreadsheet does not change what a person decides about his own career.

natural: No. It changes what we are obliged to do about it, and the obligation is the only part I control.
plain: That is true. But the number does change what the project must do about the risk. That obligation is the only part the Project Manager controls.

natural: While we are in the log. Release 1 scored Risk at sixty-eight per cent, amber, on one finding. The Committee approved the response to R-07 in October last year. It is in the minutes. It is not in the Risk Log. Half a person-day, yours, and the finding is six months old.
plain: While we are in the log. My Release 1 review scored the Risk area at 68 per cent, amber, because of one finding. In October 2026 the Steering Committee approved the response to R-07. That approval is in the meeting minutes but not in the Risk Log. Correcting it takes half a person-day of your time, and the finding is now six months old.

natural: It goes in today.
plain: The Project Manager will write it into the Risk Log today.

natural: You said that in April. Minutes are the record of a meeting. The log is the record of the risk, and only one of those is read by somebody who was not there.
plain: You said that in April. Minutes record what a meeting did. The Risk Log records the risk itself. Only the log is read by people who were not in the meeting.

natural: Then the fourth step, and it is the one that quietly kills projects. Strategy on R-07 is Reduce. Two actions. The key-person clause in the contract of the eighteenth of September, and fifteen person-days of knowledge transfer, task four point seven, target the eighteenth of December last year.
plain: Next comes step four of risk management: checking that the planned response is actually being carried out. This is the step projects most often skip. The response strategy for R-07 is Reduce. It has two actions. First, the key-person clause in the contract signed on 18 September 2026. Second, 15 person-days of knowledge transfer, which is task 4.7 in the Work Plan, with a target date of 18 December 2026.

natural: Two of the three modules were transferred.
plain: Two of the three parts of that knowledge transfer were done.

natural: And the third?
plain: What happened to the third part?

natural: December was busy. January was worse. It is scheduled.
plain: December was a busy month and January was worse. The third part is in the schedule.

natural: It is scheduled for the week of the fourteenth of February. The third one is the product configuration engine. Two people in Europe can change a pricing rule in it without breaking a repayment schedule, and Ada is not one of them.
plain: It is scheduled for the week of 14 February, which has already passed. The third part is the product configuration engine, where a new loan product is set up by settings instead of new code. Only two people in Europe can change a pricing rule there without damaging a repayment schedule. Ada Lovelace is not one of them.

natural: So we have a response and we have not exercised it. Nine months past its target date, on the risk at the top of the log.
plain: So the project has a planned response but has not carried it out. It is nine months past its target date, and it belongs to the highest risk in the log.

natural: Write it at five and somebody upstairs makes him give me the fortnight.
plain: If you record the likelihood as 5, senior management will force Leonardo to give me the two weeks I need.

natural: I am not scoring a risk to win an argument about a calendar.
plain: I will not change a risk score in order to win an argument about the schedule.

natural: Last one and I will save it. R-11, the Levallois accelerators, six weeks down to four on a new instrument. It is still sitting at Proposed and somebody has typed Reduce in the strategy column.
plain: One more before saving. Risk R-11 is about tools from Levallois Systems that could reduce onboarding of a new lending product from 6 weeks to 4. Its status is still Proposed, and somebody has entered Reduce as its response strategy.

natural: Enhance. It is the only good news in there and it is filed as a threat.
plain: The correct strategy is Enhance. R-11 is an opportunity, not a threat, and it is the only positive entry in the log.

natural: Close it. Enhance is a verb that needs a person attached to it. Show me the person and I withdraw the objection.
plain: Close R-11. Enhance means somebody has to do the work. Show me the person who will do it, and I will withdraw my objection.

natural: And R-07 stays mine.
plain: And I remain the owner of risk R-07.

natural: The owner is whoever can act on it. On this one that was never going to be me.
plain: The risk owner is the person who can actually do something about the risk. For R-07 that was never the Project Manager.

natural: The log is saved at 09:41. R-07: likelihood four, impact five, risk level twenty, escalation yes, strategy Reduce, owner Leonardo da Vinci, status Approved. On the twenty-eighth of September 2027 it is still, in every sense the guide means, a risk. Tesla leaves first and takes the stairs.
plain: The Risk Log is saved at 09:41. R-07 now reads: likelihood 4, impact 5, risk level 20, escalation yes, strategy Reduce, owner Leonardo da Vinci, status Approved. On 28 September 2027 it is still a risk in the full sense of the word. Tesla leaves the room first and takes the stairs.

natural: Gustave Eiffel is in the project room before the ceiling lights have finished coming on. He does not sit down and he does not open his laptop. There is one printed page on the table in front of him.
plain: Gustave Eiffel is in the project room before the ceiling lights have fully switched on. He does not sit down and he does not open his laptop. One printed page lies on the table in front of him.

natural: Yesterday, sixteen forty. To me, copied to our people in Stockholm. His notice runs to the thirtieth of November.
plain: He sent his resignation yesterday at 16:40. He sent it to me and copied it to our head office in Stockholm. His notice period ends on 30 November.

natural: Where.
plain: Where is he going?

natural: A clearing house in Frankfurt. I telephoned him at seven this morning and offered money. It is not money.
plain: He is going to a clearing house in Frankfurt. I telephoned him at 07:00 this morning and offered more money. Money is not the reason he is leaving.

natural: Leonardo arrives with his coat still on and hears the last nine words of it from the doorway.
plain: Leonardo comes in still wearing his coat. He hears the last part of the sentence from the doorway.

natural: Then buy him out. Pay him to sit in that chair until Christmas.
plain: Then pay him to stay. Pay him to remain in that seat until Christmas.

natural: He is serving a notice, not for sale. And he is my employee, which is not the same as my asset.
plain: He is working his notice period. He cannot be bought. He is an employee of Levallois, and an employee is not a piece of property.

natural: At twenty past eight Tesla comes in with two coffees and puts one down in front of the Project Manager. Eiffel turns the printed page face down, which is the only gentle thing anyone does all morning.
plain: At 08:20 Tesla comes in carrying two coffees. He puts one of them in front of the Project Manager. Eiffel turns the printed resignation letter face down on the table. It is the only kind act of the morning.

natural: One of those is yours. I am not apologising for anything.
plain: One coffee is for you. I will not apologise for resigning.

natural: Two people can change a pricing rule in that engine without breaking a repayment schedule. That has been true since January. I said so in January.
plain: Only two people can change a pricing rule in that engine without damaging a repayment schedule. That has been true since January. I said so in January.

natural: You said so a week ago as well.
plain: He said the same thing a week ago, at the risk review.

natural: And you left it at four.
plain: And the Project Manager kept the likelihood score at 4.

natural: What does it change on your screen? Say it in one sentence, because I have Florence at nine.
plain: What changes in your records? Say it in one sentence, because I meet Florence at 09:00.

natural: R-07 asks me for a likelihood. Give me one.
plain: The Risk Log entry R-07 needs a likelihood score. Give me one.

natural: One hundred per cent.
plain: The likelihood is 100 per cent.

natural: The column stops at five, and five is very high. There is no value on it that means it happened on Monday at twenty to five.
plain: The likelihood column only goes up to 5, and 5 means very high. No number on that scale means the event has already happened, which it did at 16:40 on Monday.

natural: On my last project we put it at five and carried on. Nobody died.
plain: On Eiffel's previous project they set the likelihood to 5 and continued as before. Nothing terrible happened.

natural: There is a clause. We paid for a clause.
plain: There is a key-person clause in the contract. The project paid for it.

natural: There is, and it worked in April. It names the platform architect in our delivery organisation and it got you a replacement and three weeks of handover at our cost. Nikola is on framework days, seconded into your team. The clause was drafted before he was ever on this project.
plain: The clause exists and it worked in April. It covers the platform architect employed in Levallois's delivery team. In April it produced a replacement and three weeks of handover, paid by Levallois. Tesla is different: he works under framework day-rates and is seconded into the ESM team. The clause was written before he joined this project.

natural: Half of your mitigation was a man. Men resign. It is in the literature.
plain: Half of your response to this risk was one person, and that person was me. People resign. That is well known.

natural: Urgency five. Impact five, because the seventeenth of December is behind it and the parallel run is behind that. Size four.
plain: The Project Manager scores the new issue. Urgency 5. Impact 5, because Release 2 on 17 December depends on it, and the parallel run depends on Release 2. Size 4.

natural: Forty person-days. That is not wrong. It is optimistic.
plain: Size 4 means about 40 person-days of work. That estimate is not incorrect, but it is hopeful.

natural: Then here is what I want. Leave R-07 where it is until the fifteenth of November. If Levallois names somebody, the risk was managed, and nobody upstairs is told the same bad news twice.
plain: This is what I want. Keep R-07 in the Risk Log until 15 November. If Levallois names a replacement architect by then, the risk was handled, and senior management does not hear the same bad news twice.

natural: And if they do not name anyone?
plain: And if Levallois does not name anyone?

natural: Then you were right and it has cost you six weeks of log entries. I can live with that. Can you?
plain: Then you were right, and the only cost is six weeks of extra work on the logs. I can accept that. Can you?

natural: The Steering Committee meets on the eighteenth. Whatever is on the screen that morning is what it will be told, and nothing else exists.
plain: The Project Steering Committee meets on 18 October. It will only be told what is on the screen that morning. Anything not recorded does not exist for that meeting.

natural: Then write it so that in five years the two entries can still find each other. And put my name on both of them.
plain: Then write it so that in five years somebody can still trace one entry from the other. And put my name on both entries.

natural: There is a leaving lunch. It is on the twenty-ninth of November and you are on the list.
plain: A farewell lunch has already been arranged for 29 November, and you are on the list.

natural: Nobody has asked for anything. You would be requesting a change to a date that has not moved, to fix a problem you have not written down.
plain: Nobody has requested a change. You would be asking to change a date that has not moved yet, in order to solve a problem that is not recorded anywhere.

natural: Then on Wednesday two people update two entries about one man, and by Christmas the two entries disagree.
plain: Then every Wednesday two people will update two records about the same person, and by Christmas the two records will contradict each other.

natural: Item three of the Steering Committee, eleven minutes allocated. Gustave Eiffel is invited for this item only and sits at the corner of the table where contractors sit.
plain: This is item three on the Steering Committee agenda, with 11 minutes allocated to it. Gustave Eiffel is invited only for this item. He sits at the corner of the table where contractors sit.

natural: Read it as it is written. Not as you would like it to sound.
plain: Read the entry exactly as it is written in the log. Do not soften the words.

natural: I-14. Lead solution architect resigns, last working day the thirtieth of November. Materialisation of risk R-07, closed on the fifth. Urgency five, impact five, size four. Owner Leonardo da Vinci. Target date the fifteenth of November. Escalation yes.
plain: Issue I-14. The lead solution architect has resigned and his last working day is 30 November. This is the materialisation of risk R-07, which was closed on 5 October. Urgency 5, impact 5, size 4. The issue owner is Leonardo da Vinci. The target date is 15 November. It is escalated.

natural: Does the seventeenth of December move?
plain: Will Release 2 slip from 17 December?

natural: Not yet.
plain: Not at this stage.

natural: That is not an answer.
plain: That is not a real answer.

natural: It is the honest one on the eighteenth of October. Ask me on the fifteenth of November and you will get an answer.
plain: It is the honest answer on 18 October. Ask the same question on 15 November and there will be a real answer.

natural: Everyone in this room has said the word architect. Do you need a person, or do you need what is in his head by the thirtieth of November?
plain: Everybody in this room has used the word architect. Which do you need: a person in the role, or the knowledge in his head, transferred before 30 November?

natural: Both. Only one of them is available.
plain: The project needs both. Only one of the two is possible now.

natural: The Architecture Office offered me a design authority for eight weeks. I said no. I will not put an ESM architect inside a design ESM is buying.
plain: The Architecture Office offered me one of its architects as design authority for eight weeks. I refused. I will not have an ESM architect designing a platform that ESM is buying from a supplier.

natural: What happens to my parallel run if December moves?
plain: What happens to the parallel run if Release 2 moves from December?

natural: It compresses. Eighth of January to the thirtieth of April, cutover the fifteenth of May. There is no slack between those two dates, so any slack has to be found in front of December.
plain: The parallel run gets shorter. It runs from 8 January to 30 April, and the switch to the new system is on 15 May. There is no spare time between those dates. Any spare time must be found before December.

natural: And I train forty people in those same weeks, while all forty of them are doing their day jobs.
plain: And I must train 40 loan administrators in those same weeks, while all of them continue their normal work.

natural: Then here is what this committee does with an issue. It does not solve it. It names who solves it, and by when, and it does that in eleven minutes.
plain: This is what this committee does with an issue. It does not solve the issue. It names the person who must solve it and the date by which it must be solved, and it does that within its 11 minutes.

natural: Three costed options sit in the pack, tabbed, prepared until eleven o'clock last night. Nobody opens the pack.
plain: The meeting pack contains three costed options with tabs, prepared until 23:00 the previous night. Nobody opens it.

natural: Leonardo, you own it. Levallois names a replacement by the fifteenth of November and hands over at Levallois's cost. Nikola's last six weeks are knowledge capture. No new design work, none, whatever he starts on Monday.
plain: Leonardo, you own this issue. Levallois must name a replacement architect by 15 November and pay for the handover itself. Nikola's last six weeks are for capturing knowledge only. No new design work, whatever he starts on Monday.

natural: He will hate that.
plain: He will strongly dislike that.

natural: Yes.
plain: Yes, he will.

natural: Understood. I report weekly to the Project Manager, and to this committee if the date slips.
plain: Understood. I will report every week to the Project Manager, and to this committee if the 15 November date is missed.

natural: Then it is D-11 as well. Decision owner Leonardo, escalation yes, people present as minuted, decision date today.
plain: The Project Manager records it in the Decision Log as D-11. The decision owner is Leonardo. It is escalated. The people present are taken from the minutes. The decision date is today.

natural: Not today. I sign it when Levallois's written confirmation is on my desk. The twenty-fifth.
plain: Not today. I will sign it when Levallois has confirmed it in writing. That will be 25 October.

natural: Decision date the twenty-fifth of October. Application date the twenty-sixth. Communicated to this committee, the Core Team and Levallois.
plain: So the decision date is 25 October and the date it takes effect is 26 October. It will be communicated to this committee, the Project Core Team and Levallois.

natural: Two logs and a third line, for one man leaving a job.
plain: That means entries in two logs and a third record, all because one person is changing employer.

natural: And nothing in that log ever says whether the decision worked.
plain: And the Decision Log never records whether the decision turned out well.

natural: No. There is no status on a decision. It is taken on one date, it applies from another, and after that it is simply true.
plain: No. A decision has no status column. It is taken on one date, it applies from another date, and after that it is a fact.

natural: The minutes go out at 16:20. D-11 is signed on the twenty-fifth, four hours after Levallois's written confirmation arrives from Stockholm. Marie Curie writes the two parallel-run dates on the back of her agenda and keeps it.
plain: The minutes are circulated at 16:20. Decision D-11 is signed on 25 October, four hours after Levallois's written confirmation arrives from Stockholm. Marie Curie writes the two parallel-run dates on the back of her agenda and keeps the paper.

natural: Deming runs the mid-Release 2 review with the checklist open on one screen and the March findings on the other. It is a habit that makes people uncomfortable and is meant to.
plain: Deming runs the quality review in the middle of Release 2. The Quality Review Checklist is open on one screen and the findings from March are open on the other. This habit makes people uncomfortable, which is why he does it.

natural: Release 1 closed at nought point eight two. Amber. Two recommendations. One was done on Friday, six months late. One is not done at all.
plain: The Release 1 review gave an overall score of 0.82, which is amber. It made two recommendations. One was completed on Friday, six months late. The other has not been done.

natural: The Levallois status report. Due by the fifth of the month. Eleventh in July, ninth in August, twelfth in September, and today is the twenty-sixth and I do not have October.
plain: The outstanding one is the contractor's monthly status report. It is due by the fifth of each month. It arrived on the 11th in July, the 9th in August and the 12th in September. Today is 26 October and the October report has not arrived.

natural: Then it stays open and I will read it out again in December.
plain: Then the finding stays open, and I will report it again in December.

natural: I have a worse one.
plain: I have a more serious problem.

natural: Break handling is built against nought point nine of the interface spec. Marie signed one point two in June. Four rules changed in between and two of them are the ones that matter.
plain: Levallois built the handling of reconciliation breaks against version 0.9 of the interface specification. Marie Curie approved version 1.2 in June. Four rules changed between the two versions, and two of those four are important.

natural: I sent them the file. In March. As an attachment, with the best possible intentions.
plain: I sent Levallois that file in March. I sent it as an email attachment, and I meant to help.

natural: Nobody says anything for a moment. Tesla has thirty-five days left on the project.
plain: Nobody speaks for a moment. Tesla has 35 days left before he leaves the project.

natural: Then it was never a specification. It was a file. The repository holds one point two, signed, with a version history and a named approver. What Levallois has is called reconciliation spec final v2.
plain: Then it was never a specification. It was only a file. That is what configuration management is for. The repository holds version 1.2, approved, with a version history and a named approver. The document Levallois is using is called reconciliation spec final v2.

natural: How much?
plain: How much will it cost to correct?

natural: Twenty-two person-days and a re-test of break handling. It does not touch December if we start on Monday.
plain: 22 person-days of work and a repeat of the tests on break handling. Release 2 on 17 December is safe if the work starts on Monday.

natural: Root cause before corrective action. Nobody here broke a rule they knew about.
plain: Find the root cause before deciding on corrective action. Nobody in this room broke a rule that they knew existed.

natural: One repository. One naming convention. Levallois pulls from it under their own account from Monday, and nothing leaves this floor as an attachment again.
plain: The corrective action is one document repository and one naming rule. From Monday Levallois will take documents from that repository using its own account. No specification will be sent as an email attachment again.

natural: And write down that we found it, not only that we fixed it. Otherwise you will find it again in March and think it is new.
plain: And record that we found this problem, not only that we corrected it. Otherwise you will find it again in March and think it is new.

natural: Which part of this is mine? I am asking honestly. My division built the wrong thing from a file my own architect sent.
plain: Which part of this is my responsibility? I am asking honestly. My division built the wrong thing from a file that my own architect sent.

natural: The quality of what your division builds. On this process you are the accountable one and I am the responsible one.
plain: The quality of what his division builds is his. On the Manage Quality process the Solution Provider is Accountable and the Project Manager is Responsible.

natural: Since when?
plain: Since when has that been the case?

natural: Since page eighty. It surprises every Solution Provider I have ever said it to.
plain: It is on page 80 of the guide. Every Solution Provider I have told is surprised by it.

natural: Then I accept it, and I would like it minuted that I accepted it before I understood it.
plain: Then I accept it. And I would like the minutes to record that I accepted it before I understood it.

natural: And it turns over one floor down. Quality Assurance: I am the accountable one, the Core Team is responsible for the evidence, and your division is informed.
plain: The letters are the other way round for the neighbouring process. On Quality Assurance the Project Manager is Accountable, the Project Core Team is Responsible for producing the evidence, and the Solution Provider is only Informed.

natural: My part does not move either way. I set the standard and I review against it. I assist. I have never signed anything on this project and I do not intend to start.
plain: Deming's own role does not change in either process. He sets the quality standard and reviews work against it. He assists. He has never signed a project document here and does not plan to.

natural: I have signed both kinds of paper this year and nobody told me they were different.
plain: I have signed both kinds of quality document this year, and nobody told me that the two were different.

natural: Then somebody puts a name on the Quality Assurance evidence pack for the December acceptance, and I would like to know whose before I spend three days compiling it.
plain: Then somebody must sign the Quality Assurance evidence pack for the acceptance in December. I want to know whose name it will be before I spend three days assembling it.

natural: Gutenberg writes the new rule on a card and tapes it to the door of the print room. Nothing travels as an attachment. It is still there in 2031.
plain: Gutenberg writes the new rule on a card and tapes it to the print room door. The rule is that no document travels as an email attachment. The card is still there in 2031.

natural: Correct. It also means that when I find something in December I am finding it against you, and not for you. Everybody prefers the other arrangement.
plain: That is correct. It also means that when I find something in December, I am finding it against you, not for you. Everybody prefers the other arrangement.

natural: I would sign it. And then Deming audits my division's work against a pack my division wrote and I countersigned, and even I can see what that looks like from the seventh floor.
plain: I would sign it. And then Deming would audit my division's work using a pack that my division wrote and I countersigned. Even I can see how that looks from the seventh floor.

natural: Then who reviews me? I set the standards and I review the outputs. If I also certify that the outputs met my standards, the review has quietly become a self-assessment.
plain: Then who reviews me? I set the standards and I review the outputs. If I also certify that the outputs met my own standards, the review becomes a self-assessment.

natural: They approved a plan in June 2026. You are asking eight people who have never opened a test log to certify that we followed it.
plain: The Steering Committee approved a plan in June 2026. You would be asking eight people who have never looked at a test log to certify that the project followed that plan.

natural: The call comes in at 08:22 from a Stockholm number. Levallois's account director, met twice before, both times at a signing. He is warm, he is quick, and inside ninety seconds he has offered a replacement architect by the fifteenth and two senior test engineers by the end of the month, if this can stay, as he puts it, at principal level.
plain: A call comes at 08:22 from a Stockholm number. It is the account director of Levallois Systems. The Project Manager has met him twice, both times at a contract signing. He is friendly and fast. Within 90 seconds he offers a replacement architect by 15 November and two senior test engineers by the end of the month, if the discussion stays, in his words, at senior level.

natural: Meaning without Gustave.
plain: That means without Gustave Eiffel taking part.

natural: He says something about Gustave being stretched. It is true, and that is what makes the offer difficult.
plain: He says that Eiffel is overloaded. That is true, which is what makes the offer tempting.

natural: You took his call.
plain: You accepted his telephone call.

natural: I listened to it. There is a difference and I would like to keep it.
plain: I listened to it, but I promised nothing. That difference matters and I want to keep it.

natural: He can find you two engineers because he can move them off another client. In February he moves them off you, and you will not hear it from him. You will hear it from me, four weeks late, in a report you already think arrives late.
plain: He can find you two engineers by taking them from another client. In February he will take them away from you. He will not tell you. You will hear it from me, four weeks later, in the report that you already think arrives late.

natural: Which brings us to the report. Due by the fifth. Today is the ninth.
plain: That brings up the monthly contractor report. It is due by the fifth of the month. Today is the ninth.

natural: At noon. It is our finance people, not our test people. Which does not make it better. Only different.
plain: It will arrive at midday. The delay is caused by Levallois's finance team, not its test team. That does not make it acceptable, only different.

natural: I have finished with their test evidence. Three of the five acceptance criteria have traceable coverage. Two are asserted.
plain: I have finished checking Levallois's test evidence. Three of the five acceptance criteria can be traced to tests. The other two are claimed but not evidenced.

natural: Which two.
plain: Which two criteria are not evidenced?

natural: AC-01 and AC-04. Onboarding in six weeks, and same-day reconciliation with no unexplained breaks.
plain: AC-01 and AC-04. AC-01 is onboarding a new product in six weeks. AC-04 is same-day reconciliation with zero unexplained differences.

natural: AC-04 needs a rollover to test it against, and there is not one until April.
plain: AC-04 can only be tested during a bond rollover, and the next one is in April.

natural: At ten past nine Lorenzo de' Medici comes down to the project room rather than summoning anyone up to the seventh floor, which in this building is a signal.
plain: At 09:10 Lorenzo de' Medici comes down to the project room instead of calling people up to the seventh floor. In this organisation that is a deliberate signal.

natural: I signed the platform contract in September of last year. I am now told that makes me accountable for how it is run, which nobody mentioned at the time.
plain: I signed the platform contract in September 2026. I have now been told that this makes me Accountable for how the outsourcing is managed. Nobody told me that when I signed.

natural: It caught the whole Committee out in Planning. The Outsourcing Plan is the same letter, in the same place, for the same reason.
plain: The same rule surprised the whole Steering Committee during Planning. The Outsourcing Plan carries the same accountability, for the same reason.

natural: Then tell me the exposure in the only two units I use. Money and time.
plain: Then tell me the exposure in the only two measures I use: money and time.
