natural: Money is contained. Payments follow release acceptance, so nothing has been paid for Release 2. Timesheets are signed monthly and they are current. Time is the exposure. A name on the fifteenth, and Nikola stops on the thirtieth whatever the name is.
plain: The money risk is limited. Payments are only made when a release is accepted, so nothing has been paid for Release 2. Timesheets are signed every month and are up to date. Time is the real exposure. A replacement architect must be named on 15 November, and Tesla leaves on 30 November whatever happens.

natural: And what do you want from me?
plain: And what do you want from me?

natural: Nothing today.
plain: Nothing today.

natural: Good answer. Accountable is not on call. If this ends in a contractual remedy it becomes mine, and on that day I will want a file, not a telephone call.
plain: Good answer. Being Accountable does not mean being available for daily problems. If this ends in a contract penalty, it becomes mine, and on that day I will want a documented file, not a telephone call.

natural: Then give me the file. In writing, dated, against the working methods in the Outsourcing Plan. I would rather be squeezed on paper by a client than reorganised by my own account director.
plain: Then give me that file. In writing, dated, and set against the working methods in the Outsourcing Plan. I would rather be pressed formally by a client than reorganised by my own account director.

natural: And tell Ada to stop mailing their test lead directly.
plain: And tell Ada Lovelace to stop emailing the contractor's test lead directly.

natural: She copies Gustave.
plain: She copies Gustave Eiffel on those emails.

natural: Copying is not asking.
plain: Sending a copy is not the same as going through him.

natural: It is not the emails. It is that my test lead now believes he has two clients and neither of them writes his objectives.
plain: The problem is not the emails. My test lead now thinks he has two clients, and neither of them sets his objectives.

natural: The letter goes out at 16:40, dated, copied to Stockholm, four paragraphs, none of them warm. The status report arrives at 12:04. The replacement architect is named at ten past four on the afternoon of the fifteenth.
plain: The letter is sent at 16:40. It is dated, copied to Levallois head office, and four paragraphs long. None of it is friendly. The monthly status report arrives at 12:04. The replacement architect is named at 16:10 on 15 November, the deadline day.

natural: Send it today and copy my management. A demand from a client is worth four of my own escalations, and by Friday you will have your architect or you will have my report saying why not.
plain: Send it today and copy my management. A formal demand from a client carries more weight than four internal escalations from me. By Friday you will have your architect, or you will have my report explaining why not.

natural: Then next month you ask me why my report does not match what you were promised, and I will not be able to tell you, because nobody will have told me either.
plain: Then next month you will ask me why my report does not match the promises you were given. I will not be able to answer, because nobody will have told me either.

natural: You would be taking a contract action in my name, in November, over a deliverable nobody has yet failed to deliver. Ask procurement what that costs us at the next tender.
plain: You would be taking contractual action in my name, in November, about a deliverable that nobody has yet failed to deliver. Ask the procurement team what that costs us at the next tender.

natural: And when it happens again in February, who do I call then? I have one call of that kind on this contract. You are asking me to spend it on a staffing gap your own route has not been given four days to close.
plain: And if it happens again in February, who do I call then? I have one call of that kind on this contract. You are asking me to use it on a staffing problem that your own route has not had four days to solve.

natural: Release 2 goes to acceptance at 14:00 on the last Friday before the building empties. Straight-through disbursement, on the date printed in the Business Case twenty-one months ago.
plain: Release 2 is handed over for acceptance at 14:00 on the last Friday before the holidays. It delivers straight-through processing of disbursements, on the exact date written in the Business Case 21 months earlier.

natural: Deployed at two. Release notes, User Manual, Operations Manual, training material. One platform and four supporting deliverables.
plain: It was deployed at 14:00. With it come release notes, a User Manual, an Operations Manual and training material. That is one main deliverable and four supporting ones.

natural: The design authority named on the release notes joined Levallois on the fifteenth of November. Nobody in the room has met him.
plain: The architect named on the release notes started at Levallois on 15 November. Nobody in the room has met him.

natural: Marie signs the lot. She is the User Representative and she is the one who will live in it.
plain: Marie signs all of it. She is the User Representative and she will use the system every day.

natural: No.
plain: No.

natural: That is the first time in two years you have not wanted a signature.
plain: That is the first time in two years that you have not wanted a signature.

natural: I want the one that is mine. I cannot tell you whether a restart procedure at two in the morning is correct, and if I sign that it is, somebody at two in the morning will believe me.
plain: I want only the document that is mine. I cannot judge whether a restart procedure at 02:00 is correct. If I sign that it is, somebody working at 02:00 will believe me.

natural: Then it goes where it belongs. Leonardo's support line takes the Operations Manual.
plain: So each document goes to the right reviewer. Leonardo's support and maintenance team reviews the Operations Manual.

natural: They will read it, they will complain about the date, and they will be right to.
plain: They will read it, they will complain about the timing, and they will be justified.

natural: Training material comes to the training function under my plan. Not to Ada, who wrote half of it, and not to Marie because she is the nearest user.
plain: The training material goes to the training function under the Business Implementation Plan. It does not go to Ada Lovelace, who wrote half of it, and it does not go to Marie Curie just because she is the closest user.

natural: Release notes to the service desk. They are the only people who read them at eight in the morning with somebody shouting.
plain: The release notes go to the service desk. They are the only people who read release notes at 08:00 while somebody is shouting at them.

natural: I have run the controls. Most of them, which is how it is meant to work. Two acceptance criteria still rest on Levallois's own test evidence and that is written down.
plain: I have carried out the quality controls, most of them myself, which is how the process should work. Two acceptance criteria still depend on Levallois's own test evidence, and I have recorded that.

natural: So what do I actually do this afternoon? In verbs.
plain: So what do I actually do this afternoon? Tell me in actions.

natural: You accept, deliverable by deliverable, on a signed note. I get them in front of you in a state worth signing.
plain: You accept each deliverable separately, on a signed Deliverables Acceptance Note. My job is to put them in front of you in a condition worth signing.

natural: And when they are not in that state?
plain: And what happens when a deliverable is not in a condition worth signing?

natural: Then the defect goes on the note with a date against it and you accept the rest. That is in the guide. It is not a favour I invented in Planning.
plain: Then the defect is written on the note with a date for fixing it, and you accept the rest. That rule is in the guide. I did not invent it during Planning.

natural: Say that again in April.
plain: Say that again in April.

natural: Two loan administrators, full time, from the eighth of January. That is not a favour either. Acceptance runs on my people or it does not run.
plain: I am giving you two loan administrators, full time, from 8 January. That is not a favour either. The acceptance testing depends on my staff.

natural: Then put the dates in the minutes. All of them, including the ones nobody likes.
plain: Then put all the dates in the minutes, including the ones nobody likes.

natural: Parallel run, eighth of January to the thirtieth of April. And there is a three billion euro EFSF maturity on the twenty-fifth of April, refinancing settling two days later. It is the heaviest reconciliation this platform will ever do and it falls in the last week.
plain: The parallel run goes from 8 January to 30 April. A 3 billion euro EFSF bond matures on 25 April and is replaced by a new one, which settles two days later. That bond rollover produces the heaviest reconciliation the platform will ever handle, and it happens in the final week.

natural: Is that not a scheduling failure on somebody's part?
plain: Is that not a planning mistake by somebody?

natural: It is a scheduling choice. This committee approved the acceptance strategy and the schedule in 2026, and the schedule follows the deliveries. Avoid every funding event and we accept in August with nobody in the building.
plain: It is a deliberate choice. The Steering Committee approved the acceptance approach and schedule in 2026, and the schedule follows the delivery dates. If the project avoided every funding event, acceptance would happen in August when almost nobody is at work.

natural: August is beautiful in this building. Eleven people and a vending machine.
plain: August is quiet and pleasant in this building. Eleven people and one vending machine.

natural: Then I sign four notes and go home. Is that the end of it?
plain: Then I sign four notes and go home. Is that the end of it?

natural: It is the end of Release 2. Final acceptance is not this signature and it is not this phase.
plain: It is the end of Release 2 only. Final project acceptance is a different signature, in a different phase.

natural: The notes are signed at 17:40. Outside, the Kirchberg is already dark and the tram is running on the winter timetable. R-09 is still open in the Risk Log at four by three, and nobody mentions it.
plain: The acceptance notes are signed at 17:40. Outside it is already dark and the tram is on the winter timetable. Risk R-09, the parallel run overlapping a bond rollover, is still open with likelihood 4 and impact 3. Nobody mentions it.

natural: Eleventh week of the parallel run. On the wall behind Grace Hopper's desk there is a printed grid of forty names, and twenty-eight of them are ticked in pencil.
plain: This is the eleventh week of the parallel run. On the wall behind Grace Hopper's desk hangs a printed grid of 40 names. 28 of them are ticked in pencil.

natural: Twelve left. Six of those are on rollover preparation until the end of April, and two are seconded to Finance and Control until June.
plain: 12 people are still untrained. Six of them are working on the bond rollover until the end of April. Two are lent to Finance and Control until June.

natural: The checklist run is the thirtieth of April. Check sixteen.
plain: The Business Implementation Checklist is run on 30 April. Check 16 is the relevant one.

natural: I know what check sixteen asks. I wrote the plan it checks.
plain: I know what check 16 asks. I wrote the Business Implementation Plan that the check tests.

natural: And training is the smaller half of it. Under the old system I chase breaks. Under the new one the system chases them and I approve or reject what it found. Same job title, same grade, different job.
plain: Training is the smaller part of the change. In the old system I search for reconciliation breaks myself. In the new one the system finds them and I approve or reject what it found. That is exception handling. Same job title, same grade, different job.

natural: Which is in the plan as a source of resistance, in your name, since 2026. It is the most honest line in the document.
plain: That is recorded in the Business Implementation Plan as a source of resistance, under Marie's name, since 2026. It is the most honest line in the document.

natural: I am not resisting. Two of my colleagues are about to discover that the interesting hour of their day has been automated, and one of them will mind very much.
plain: I am not resisting. Two of my colleagues will soon find that the most interesting hour of their day has been automated, and one of them will be very unhappy.

natural: And the disbursement procedure has to be republished with segregation of duties enforced by the platform instead of by two people remembering. That goes through Legal and past Internal Audit, and it is not a project task. It is mine.
plain: And the disbursement procedure must be republished, with segregation of duties enforced by the platform instead of by two people remembering. It has to go through Legal and then Internal Audit. That is not project work. It is mine.

natural: What can I take off you?
plain: What work can the Project Manager remove from her?

natural: Say the rest of the sentence first. The part you have been circling since you came up the stairs.
plain: Finish the sentence first. The part you have been avoiding since you came up the stairs.

natural: It is not mine to take. On this one you are responsible, Florence is accountable, and I support.
plain: He cannot take the work. On Manage Business Implementation the Business Manager is Responsible, the Project Owner is Accountable, and the Project Manager only Supports.

natural: And I am the accountable one, and I have no spare person in this division before the fifteenth of May. So do not say the word as though it solves anything.
plain: And I am the Accountable one, and I have no spare person in this division before 15 May. So do not use the word as though it solves anything.

natural: Rooms. Slots in the Work Plan with dates on them. Ada two days a week until the end of April. The Core Team for demonstrations. And the reporting, so that nobody upstairs can say afterwards that they did not know.
plain: Rooms. Dated slots in the Project Work Plan. Ada Lovelace for two days a week until the end of April. The Core Team for demonstrations. And the status reporting, so that nobody in senior management can say afterwards that they did not know.

natural: I can rebuild the exception walkthrough as four sessions of fifty minutes instead of one afternoon. Then it fits in the gaps around a settlement.
plain: I can rebuild the exception-handling walkthrough as four sessions of 50 minutes instead of one long afternoon. Then it fits into the gaps around a bond settlement.

natural: That helps. That is genuinely the shape of the problem.
plain: That helps. That is genuinely the shape of the problem.

natural: Put my two in the first one. If they hear it from Ada before they hear it from a rumour, half of it goes away.
plain: Put my two colleagues in the first session. If they hear it from Ada before they hear a rumour, half of the problem disappears.

natural: And the part that is not the project's at all. Refresher training from 2029, Lending Operations. Business continuity for the platform, Lending Operations. Benefits against the five success criteria, quarterly, from the first quarter of 2029, Lending Operations.
plain: And here is the part that is not the project's at all. Refresher training from 2029: Lending Operations. Business continuity for the platform: Lending Operations. Measuring the five success criteria every quarter from the first quarter of 2029: Lending Operations.

natural: You keep handing me things.
plain: You keep giving me more things to carry.

natural: The guide is blunt about it. This work is almost always still required long after the project has ended, and by then there is no project to do it.
plain: The guide is direct about this. Business implementation work is nearly always needed long after the project ends, and by then the project no longer exists.

natural: Meaning you leave in July and we are still becoming a different department in 2030.
plain: So you leave in July, and we are still becoming a different department in 2030.

natural: Yes.
plain: Yes.

natural: Well. At least nobody is pretending.
plain: Well. At least nobody is pretending.

natural: And on Friday I report it in amber.
plain: And on Friday the Project Manager will report this area as amber in the status report.

natural: Good. Amber is the first honest colour that plan has had since January.
plain: Good. Amber is the first truthful status that plan has had since January.

natural: Twelve names on the wall without a tick against them, and eight weeks until the platform goes live.
plain: 12 names on the wall still have no tick beside them, and the new system goes live in eight weeks.

natural: Then put Ada's four sessions in your plan with dates, and my twelve names in your report without softening them. I would rather be visible than helped.
plain: Then put Ada's four sessions in your plan with dates, and my 12 names in your report without softening them. I would rather be visible than helped.

natural: And in August, when somebody forgets which button releases a value date, they ring the person who taught them. You are gone, and my team never learnt to teach itself.
plain: And in August, when somebody forgets which button releases a value date, they will telephone the person who taught them. You will have gone, and my team will never have learnt to teach itself.

natural: We had this argument in June 2026 and I ruled on it. D-05. Reopen it now and you are not solving a training problem, you are relitigating a decision because it became expensive.
plain: We had this argument in June 2026 and I decided it. That is decision D-05. If you reopen it now, you are not solving a training problem. You are reopening a decision because it has become expensive.

natural: Slip it to September and the parallel run runs through the summer, when this floor is at half strength. You will train fewer people, not more.
plain: If you move it to September, the parallel run continues through the summer, when this floor is at half strength. You will train fewer people, not more.

natural: The three billion euro EFSF bond matured on Tuesday. The refinancing settles today, value date today, and the funding cost allocation across the pooled programme loans recomputed overnight for the first time on the new platform.
plain: A 3 billion euro EFSF bond matured on Tuesday. The new bond that replaces it settles today, with today as the value date. Last night the platform recalculated how the funding cost is shared across the pooled programme loans. It was the first time it did this.

natural: The reconciliation ran at six. Nine hundred and ninety-eight loans reconcile. Two do not.
plain: The reconciliation ran at 06:00. 998 loans match. Two do not.

natural: Which two.
plain: Which two loans?

natural: Two on the old EFSF pooling arrangement. The allocation from the rollover reaches them a day late, so this morning the platform and the treasury system disagree about the carry, and my report says so in a footnote instead of balancing.
plain: Two loans under the old EFSF pooling arrangement. The share of the rollover cost reaches them one day late. So this morning the platform and the treasury system disagree about the carrying cost. My report explains that in a footnote instead of balancing.

natural: It is the treasury feed, not the platform. The feed publishes at close, we consume at six, and for those two the recomputation lands after close.
plain: The cause is the treasury data feed, not the platform. The feed publishes at the end of the day and we read it at 06:00. For those two loans the recalculation arrives after the feed has closed.

natural: I do not care whose it is at ten past seven in the morning. My report does not reconcile, and SC2 says same day.
plain: At ten past seven in the morning I do not care which system is at fault. My report does not balance, and success criterion SC2 requires same-day reconciliation.

natural: And the calendar says the parallel run ends on Sunday, Florence approves the deployment on the fourteenth, and we cut over on the fifteenth.
plain: And the calendar: the parallel run ends on Sunday 30 April, Florence approves the deployment on 14 May, and we switch to the new system on 15 May.

natural: Ask me plainly, both of you. I have the Managing Director's office at nine and I would rather not improvise.
plain: Ask me the question clearly, both of you. I am due in the Managing Director's office at 09:00 and I do not want to improvise.

natural: I sign the Operational Readiness Review tomorrow morning either way. What I am able to sign depends on what this room decides today.
plain: I sign the Operational Readiness Review tomorrow morning in any case. What I am able to write in it depends on what this room decides today.

natural: Two of my administrators have been on acceptance runs since the eighth of January. They found this at ten past six on the one morning it mattered. That is the process working, not the process failing.
plain: Two of Grace's loan administrators have been running acceptance tests since 8 January. They found this problem at 06:10 on the one morning when it mattered. That means the process worked, not that it failed.

natural: We can force an intraday recomputation for the pooled loans and re-run at eleven. Not this morning. Four days of work and a re-test.
plain: We can force a mid-day recalculation for the pooled loans and run the reconciliation again at 11:00. Not this morning. It needs four days of work and a repeat test.

natural: Four days from today puts a clean re-test on the third of May. Inside the acceptance window, outside the parallel run.
plain: Four days from today means a clean repeat test on 3 May. That is still within the acceptance period, but after the parallel run has ended.

natural: And both breaks go in the Issue Log before nine. One entry each, owner Gustave, target the third of May. Whatever this room decides, they exist somewhere other than a footnote.
plain: Both breaks will be entered in the Issue Log before 09:00. One entry for each loan, with Gustave Eiffel as owner and a target date of 3 May. Whatever is decided here, the two breaks will exist somewhere other than a footnote.

natural: Do that first. I have been the only record of those two loans since ten past six.
plain: Do that first. Since 06:10 I have been the only record that those two loans exist.

natural: The criterion is AC-04. Same-day reconciliation, tolerance zero unexplained breaks. These two are explained. They are not resolved. The tolerance only uses one of those words.
plain: The acceptance criterion is AC-04: same-day reconciliation with a tolerance of zero unexplained breaks. These two breaks are explained, but they are not fixed. The tolerance refers only to unexplained breaks.

natural: And whatever is decided, the Deliverables Acceptance Checklist gets run tomorrow with the true answers in it. Including the ones that are not yes.
plain: And whatever is decided, the Deliverables Acceptance Checklist is completed tomorrow with true answers, including the answers that are not yes.

natural: I am not signing that this report reconciles, because it does not.
plain: I will not sign that this report reconciles, because it does not.

natural: Then tell me what you will sign. I am not carrying a refusal upstairs without a route out of it.
plain: Then tell me what you will sign. I will not take a refusal to senior management without a way out of it.

natural: Ask him. He wrote the route in May 2026 and I have been carrying it around ever since.
plain: Ask him. He wrote the procedure in May 2026, and I have kept it ever since.

natural: Nine hundred and ninety-eight, Marie.
plain: 998 loans, Marie.

natural: Nine hundred and ninety-eight is not a thousand. That is the whole of my job in one sentence.
plain: 998 is not 1,000. That is my whole job in one sentence.

natural: For what it is worth, she is right about the feed and I would not sign it either.
plain: For what it is worth, she is right about the feed, and I would not sign it either.

natural: Room Spaak, the nineteenth of May 2026. Nine hundred and ninety-eight right, two wrong, and a value date on the Thursday. She was two years early and off by nothing at all.
plain: In Room Spaak on 19 May 2026, Marie described this exact case: 998 correct, two wrong, with a value date on the Thursday. She was two years early and completely accurate.

natural: Then write both loan identifiers on the note. Not a category, not a footnote. The two numbers, so that in five years somebody can find exactly what I did and did not put my name to.
plain: Then write both loan reference numbers on the note. Not a category and not a footnote. The two numbers, so that in five years somebody can see exactly what I did and did not sign for.

natural: Then check thirteen says the deliverables meet the requirements, and it is a false statement signed by four people, one of whom is me.
plain: Then check 13 says that the deliverables meet the requirements. That is a false statement signed by four people, and I am one of them.

natural: Nine hundred and ninety-eight loans work. You would put this division back on three-day reconciliation over two of them, eighteen days from a cutover the Board has a date for.
plain: 998 loans work. You would put this division back on three-day reconciliation because of two of them, 18 days before a go-live date that the Board already has.

natural: I can. And then the only person in this institution who reads that report every morning is recorded as having no view, and the next time she has one she will keep it to herself.
plain: I can. And then the only person in this institution who reads that report every morning is recorded as having no view, and the next time she has one she will keep it to herself.

natural: Saturday the thirteenth of May: full backup of the old system, restore tested, four hours forty. Sunday: Florence Nightingale's written approval to deploy. Monday the fifteenth at 06:10 the first disbursement instruction goes into the new platform, and at 06:14 it is out the other side. Five weeks later the Steering Committee sits down under the same green glare as the last two gates.
plain: On Saturday 13 May the old system was fully backed up and the restore was tested, taking 4 hours 40 minutes. On Sunday Florence Nightingale gave written approval to deploy. On Monday 15 May, the day of the cutover, the first disbursement instruction entered the new platform at 06:10 and came out the other side at 06:14. Five weeks later the Steering Committee meets under the same green light as at the two earlier gates.

natural: Item one. Ready for Closing.
plain: Item one on the agenda is the Ready for Closing gate.

natural: Transition Checklist, cutover run, the fifteenth of May. Twenty-six checks plus the thirteen IT ones, because we answered yes to the IT question.
plain: The Transition Checklist was completed for the cutover on 15 May. It has 26 general checks plus 13 IT-specific ones, which apply because the project answered yes to the question about an IT component.

natural: Security signed on the sixth of May. Levallois's accounts revoked at cutover, project accounts removed, support access rules live since the sixteenth.
plain: Alan Turing signed the security section on 6 May. Levallois's accounts were withdrawn at cutover, project accounts were deleted, and the support access rules have applied since 16 May.

natural: Data protection the same day. The migration carried no personal data beyond named authorising officers, and the retention rule on the old archive is unchanged until decommissioning.
plain: Louis Brandeis signed the data protection section on the same day. The migration moved no personal data except the names of the officers who authorise payments. The retention rule for the old system's archive stays the same until it is decommissioned.

natural: Rollback: the old system stays warm until the thirtieth of June. Florence can order it back before the six o'clock value-date cut-off on any morning until then.
plain: On rollback: the old system stays available and ready until 30 June. Until that date Florence can order a return to it, on any morning before the 06:00 value-date deadline.

natural: Which is eight days from now, and it is the last day anybody can change their mind cheaply.
plain: That is eight days from today. It is the last day on which anyone can reverse the decision at low cost.

natural: Check twenty-four, were all the transition goals achieved. Yes, partially. Zero missed value dates since cutover. Decommissioning the old system is open, and it is not ours.
plain: Check 24 asks whether all the transition goals were achieved. The answer is Yes, partially. No value date has been missed since cutover. Decommissioning the old system is still open, and that is not the project's work.

natural: Mine, in other words.
plain: In other words, it is mine.

natural: Yours. With maintenance and support, which started at cutover, and the documentation handover, which completed on the nineteenth of May.
plain: Yes, hers. Together with maintenance and support, which began at cutover, and the handover of documentation, which was completed on 19 May.

natural: Say the part about the plan, because I watched you do it and it is the only unusual thing in this file.
plain: Tell them what you did with the plan. I watched you do it, and it is the only unusual thing in this file.

natural: We have a Transition Plan, approved here in 2026. I still walked the list the guide gives to projects that do not have one. Who is responsible. What must be true before transition is complete. Backups and rollback. Training. Delivery coordinated, communicated and accepted. Maintenance and support started. Documentation handed over.
plain: The project has a Transition Plan, approved by this committee in 2026. Even so, the Project Manager worked through the list that the guide gives to projects without such a plan. Who is responsible. What must be achieved before transition is complete. Backups and rollback. Training. Delivery coordinated, communicated and accepted. Maintenance and support started. All documentation handed over.

natural: You used a checklist meant for people without a plan.
plain: You used a list meant for projects that have no Transition Plan.

natural: As a completeness test against our own. It found one gap. Nobody had written down who starts the support contract clock, and the answer was nobody.
plain: He used it to test whether the project's own plan was complete. It found one gap. Nobody had recorded who starts the support contract period, and in fact nobody had started it.

natural: Forty administrators trained by the thirtieth of April. The two positions were re-tested on the third of May and closed. Same-day reconciliation has held every morning since the fifteenth, including a quarter-end.
plain: All 40 loan administrators were trained by 30 April. The two unreconciled loans were re-tested on 3 May and closed. Same-day reconciliation has worked every morning since 15 May, including at a quarter-end.

natural: And the issue that came out of R-07 closed on the twenty-eighth of April. Seven months open, and it closed quietly, which is how they close when they close at all.
plain: And the issue that came from risk R-07 was closed on 28 April. It was open for seven months, and it closed quietly, which is how they close when they close at all.

natural: On the transition, who was accountable? I want that on the record before this committee approves anything.
plain: On the transition, who was Accountable? I want that in the minutes before this committee approves anything.

natural: This committee. I ran it. You gave provisional acceptance on the fifth of May, before the transition, and ownership transferred on the fifteenth.
plain: This committee was Accountable. I was Responsible for running the transition. You gave provisional acceptance on 5 May, before the transition, and ownership passed to you on 15 May.

natural: Phase Exit Review Checklist, Executing sheet. Ninety-seven per cent, status nought point nine. I answered it, Deming assured the answers, and it approves nothing by itself.
plain: The Phase Exit Review Checklist for the Executing Phase: 97 per cent, status 0.9. I answered it, Deming assured the answers, and it approves nothing by itself.

natural: Deviations from the approved Business Case or the Charter?
plain: Are there any differences from the approved Business Case or the Project Charter?

natural: None. Eight point four million, three thousand one hundred person-days, twenty-six months, as approved in March 2026. SC1, SC2 and SC4 demonstrated. SC3 rehearsed in the test environment in eleven days but not proven in production, because the Treaty reform is not in force. SC5: one audit finding closed, one with Internal Audit, and they have told us early July.
plain: There are none. The budget is 8.4 million euro, the effort 3,100 person-days and the duration 26 months, as approved in March 2026. Success criteria SC1, SC2 and SC4 have been demonstrated. SC3 was rehearsed in the test environment in 11 days but has not been proved in live use, because the Treaty reform is not yet in force. For SC5, one internal audit finding is closed and the second is with Internal Audit, who expect to answer in early July.

natural: Then this gate is not mine either. Two years, and this Board has been asked for two decisions in all of it.
plain: Then this gate is not mine either. In two years this Board has been asked to take two decisions.

natural: So let me sign the final acceptance this morning and let July be the party.
plain: Then let me sign the final project acceptance this morning, and let July be the celebration.

natural: No.
plain: No.

natural: Say why, in one sentence, because I will have to repeat it to people who were not here.
plain: Say why, in one sentence, because I will have to repeat it to people who were not here.

natural: Then it is minuted as you say it. Ready for Closing, approved, the twenty-second of June 2028. Project-End Review on the twelfth of July, and I will sign the thing you will not let me sign today.
plain: Then it is minuted in those words. Ready for Closing, approved, 22 June 2028. The Project-End Review Meeting is on 12 July, and I will then sign the document you will not let me sign today.

natural: Then the Project-End Review reviews a project that has already been accepted, and every lesson it captures arrives after the only signature that could have been withheld.
plain: Then the Project-End Review examines a project that has already been accepted, and every lesson it records arrives after the only signature that could have been withheld.

natural: Internal Audit will answer on their calendar, not on yours. You would keep a project alive for weeks so that a checklist can say yes instead of yes, partially.
plain: Internal Audit answers on its own timetable, not on yours. You would keep a project alive for weeks so that a checklist can say yes instead of yes, partially.

natural: Benefits were never measurable inside twenty-six months and the Business Case said so on page four. Bring me a deviation and I will act. Do not bring me a gate.
plain: Benefits were never going to be measurable within 26 months, and the Business Case said so on page four. Bring me a deviation and I will act. Do not bring me a gate.

natural: Thirty-four degrees on the plateau and the blinds are down on the south side. Nine people, a jug of water already going warm, and Gustave Eiffel, who flew in last night and flies out at seven.
plain: It is 34 degrees outside. The blinds on the south side are closed. Nine people are in the room. There is a jug of water and it is already warm. Gustave Eiffel arrived last night. His flight home is at 19:00.

natural: The agenda went out on the fifth, with the Business Case, the Charter, the Handbook, the Work Plan, both the Transition and the Business Implementation Plans, and the four logs.
plain: The agenda was sent on 5 July. Attached to it were the Business Case, the Project Charter, the Project Handbook, the Work Plan, the Transition Plan, the Business Implementation Plan and the four project logs.

natural: I have the Minutes. I asked for them, so nobody has to look at the floor.
plain: I will write the Minutes of this meeting. I asked to do it, so that nobody else has to volunteer.

natural: Before anything. Thank you. From the Division, from the institution, and from me. I am told this is normally warmer. It is not going to be.
plain: First, thank you. Thank you from the Lending Operations Division, from the institution, and from me. People tell me that this speech is usually warmer than mine. Mine will not be.

natural: Say it to the fourth floor as well. They ran the parallel in January and nobody has been up there since May.
plain: Please say it to the fourth floor too. Those people ran the parallel test in January. Nobody has visited them since May.

natural: Monday. With names.
plain: I will do it on Monday, and I will name people.

natural: Numbers, then. Final cost eight point nine six million against eight point four baselined. Six point seven per cent over. Effort three thousand three hundred and seven person-days against three thousand one hundred.
plain: Now the numbers. The final cost was 8.96 million euro. The approved budget was 8.4 million euro. That is 6.7 per cent more. The effort was 3,307 person-days against a plan of 3,100.

natural: Nearly all of it is data migration, and data migration was mine. Say that before somebody says it kindly.
plain: Almost all of the extra cost is data migration. Data migration was my responsibility. Please say that clearly, before someone says it in a gentle way.

natural: Go-live on the fifteenth of May, which is the date in the Charter from March 2026. Scope: eleven changes approved, two postponed, one rejected. None of them touched the Business Case.
plain: The system went live on 15 May 2028. That is the date written in the Project Charter, approved in March 2026. On scope: 11 changes were approved, 2 were postponed and 1 was rejected. None of them changed the Business Case.

natural: Quality. Compliance against the Quality Management Plan, all four reviews, and I have no reservation anywhere in it. Enjoy that. I do not say it often and I will not say it twice today.
plain: Now quality. I checked the work against the Quality Management Plan across all four reviews. I have no objection anywhere. Enjoy that sentence. I do not say it often, and I will not say it again today.

natural: SC5. I was told autumn.
plain: Now SC5, the success criterion about the audit findings. I was told the answer would come in the autumn.

natural: The closure letter came on the fourth. Both findings shut. Segregation of duties, and the audit trail. They had the evidence pack since May and it held.
plain: Internal Audit sent the closure letter on 4 July 2028. Both findings are now closed: the one about who may do which step, and the one about the record of changes. The auditors had our evidence since May and it was good enough.

natural: While we are on the five. Who measures them after this month?
plain: While we are talking about the five success criteria. Who measures them after July?

natural: Item nine.
plain: That is item nine on the agenda.

natural: It is always item nine.
plain: The difficult things are always at the end of the agenda.

natural: Contractor performance. Gustave is sitting in the room. I assume that was decided and not overlooked.
plain: Now the contractor's performance. Gustave Eiffel is in the room. I assume someone decided that, and did not simply forget.

natural: Decided. We evaluate the contractor with the contractor here, or what we write down is gossip.
plain: It was decided. We assess the contractor while the contractor is present. If we do it without him, what we write is only rumour.

natural: Both releases on their baselined dates. The second one after they lost their lead architect and we lost ours. The configuration engine is better than the tender described. The migration estimate was optimistic and both signatures on it are in this room.
plain: Levallois delivered both releases on the planned dates. They delivered the second one after they had lost their lead architect and we had lost ours. The product configuration engine is better than the tender promised. The estimate for data migration was too optimistic. Both people who signed that estimate are in this room.

natural: Harder than that. We priced a migration off a data model we had never been shown. It is in our own closing note. Whoever writes our next bid will read it. Put the evaluation in today's Minutes, please — it is the only thing I take home.
plain: I will say it more strongly. We priced the data migration without ever seeing the data model. That sentence is in our own closing note. The person who writes our next offer will read it. Please put the evaluation in today's Minutes. It is the only thing I take home with me.

natural: Marie. Does it work?
plain: Marie, does the system work?

natural: Ask me in January. I have had it eight weeks and it has not seen a December.
plain: Ask me again in January. I have used it for eight weeks. It has not yet been through a December, which is our busiest time.

natural: Forty administrators retrained by the thirtieth of April. Two roles redesigned. Segregation of duties is in the platform now, not in Marie standing behind somebody at half past four.
plain: 40 loan administrators were retrained by 30 April 2028. Two jobs were redesigned. The rule about who may do which step is now enforced by the system. Before, Marie Curie enforced it by standing behind a colleague at 16:30.

natural: Then the part I have to live with. I can tell the Board of Directors that it runs. I cannot tell them what it was worth. Not one of the five survives a second question.
plain: Now the part I must accept. I can tell the Board of Directors that the system is running. I cannot tell them what it is worth. If anyone asks a second question about the five success criteria, I have no answer.

natural: Longer than this meeting. Give me until the seventeenth and I will bring you the section.
plain: That takes longer than this meeting has. Give me until 17 July and I will bring you that part of the report.

natural: Florence's assistant puts her head round the door at eleven ten. The Board of Directors preparation has moved to two. The Lessons Learned session is at half past one.
plain: At 11:10 Florence Nightingale's assistant opens the door. The Board of Directors preparation has been moved to 14:00. The Lessons Learned session starts at 13:30.

natural: Grace can hold the business side this afternoon. Do I have to sit and listen to people say what they would have done differently?
plain: Grace Hopper can represent the business side this afternoon. Do I have to sit and listen to people saying what they would have done differently?

natural: Then I move the Board preparation and I sit through all of it. But say it that way. If it is required, tell me it is required. Do not ask me as though it were a favour.
plain: Then I will move the Board preparation and stay for the whole session. But say it like that. If it is required, tell me it is required. Do not ask me as if I were doing you a favour.

natural: I represent the business side. I do not represent her. If somebody asks me this afternoon whether the Division will own benefit tracking, I cannot answer, and you know I cannot.
plain: I represent the business side. I do not represent Florence. If someone asks me this afternoon whether the Division will own the benefit measurement, I cannot answer. You know that I cannot.

natural: Then we have the same conversation twice and end with two versions of it. Half these people are on other projects by Wednesday.
plain: Then we hold the same discussion twice and we end with two different versions of it. By Wednesday half of these people are working on other projects.

natural: Then twelve subjects of the Project-End Report get written by one person who was in the room, for an approver who was not. I still have to review it, and I will write that down.
plain: Then one person who was in the room writes all twelve subjects of the Project-End Report, for an approver who was not in the room. I must still review that report, and I will record this.

natural: Half past one. The sandwiches were a mistake. Somebody opened the blinds for a photograph nobody had asked for and the room is at twenty-eight degrees. Albert Einstein has come down from the Architecture Office for the afternoon.
plain: It is 13:30. The sandwiches were a bad idea. Someone opened the blinds for a photograph that nobody wanted, and the room is now at 28 degrees. Albert Einstein has come down from the Architecture Office for the afternoon.

natural: One honest question before we start, and I am not being difficult.
plain: I have one honest question before we start. I am not trying to cause trouble.

natural: Nobody has perspective eight weeks after a go-live. September. You would get considered answers instead of tired ones.
plain: Nobody can judge a project clearly eight weeks after it goes live. Do this in September. Then you get careful answers instead of tired ones.

natural: Who is in the room in September?
plain: Who will still be here in September?

natural: Not me. Fourth floor from Monday, with a queue of my own.
plain: Not me. From Monday I am back on the fourth floor with my own work waiting.

natural: Not me. My contract ends on the thirty-first and I am on a plane at seven tonight.
plain: Not me. My contract ends on 31 July and my flight leaves at 19:00 tonight.

natural: Two of your testers go the same day.
plain: Two of the contractor's test engineers leave on the same day.

natural: I still think September gives better answers. I accept that it gives them to nobody.
plain: I still believe September would give better answers. But I accept that in September there would be nobody left to give them.

natural: We have the register in any case. Forty-one entries since Planning, each written the week the thing happened.
plain: We have the register anyway. It holds 41 entries made since the Planning Phase. Each one was written in the same week as the event it describes.

natural: Then read it out and let everybody go home.
plain: Then read the register out loud and let everyone leave.

natural: The register is what people wrote on their own. It is not what they say to each other.
plain: The register holds what each person wrote alone. That is not the same as what people say when they are together.

natural: It really is not. Entry nineteen says migration rehearsal effort underestimated. It does not say that Nikola told me in November and I assumed he was managing it himself.
plain: That is true. Entry 19 says the effort for the migration rehearsal was estimated too low. It does not say that Nikola Tesla told me about it in November, and that I assumed he was handling it himself.

natural: He was not managing it. He was rewriting it.
plain: He was not handling it. He was rewriting it.

natural: Which is a lesson, and it has just been captured, and it is twenty to two.
plain: That is a lesson. It has just been recorded. The time is 13:40.

natural: I am here because the Steering Committee was invited. I will take two of these into the target architecture review in October. That is not manners. It is the only road they travel on.
plain: I am here because the Steering Committee was invited. I will take two of these lessons into the architecture review in October. I am not being polite. That review is the only way these lessons reach other projects.

natural: Explain that to me properly. Why is a Steering Committee sitting in a room about what went wrong?
plain: Explain that properly to me. Why does a Steering Committee sit in a meeting about mistakes?

natural: Because a lesson that stays inside the project it came from is a memory. The four of you sit on six other projects between you.
plain: Because a lesson that never leaves its own project is only a memory. The four members of this committee sit on six other projects in total.

natural: There is a second guideline on that page and nobody has said it out loud.
plain: There is a second guideline on that page of the guide, and nobody has said it aloud yet.

natural: Say it.
plain: Please say it.

natural: The person running this session should not be the person the session is about.
plain: The person who leads this session should not be the person the session is about.

natural: Meaning me.
plain: You mean me.

natural: Twenty-six months of this belong to the Project Manager. If you hold the pen, half the room is kind to you and the other half aims. Give me the pen and answer when you are asked.
plain: Twenty-six months of this project belong to the Project Manager. If you lead the session, half the room will be gentle with you and the other half will attack you. Give me the pen. Then take part, and answer when someone asks you a question.

natural: I would pay to watch that.
plain: I would like to see that.

natural: I moved a Board preparation for this. Decide.
plain: I moved a Board preparation meeting so that I could be here. Make a decision.

natural: Then I take the pen. Six headings, twenty minutes each, and the Project Manager sits down and answers when asked, like everybody else in the room.
plain: Then I will lead it. Six headings, twenty minutes for each one. The Project Manager sits down and answers questions like everyone else.

natural: In September I am not an employee of Levallois. Everything I know about how you and I estimated that migration gets on a plane with me tonight.
plain: In September I no longer work for Levallois. Everything I know about how we estimated the data migration leaves with me tonight.

natural: Then entry nineteen stands as it is and nobody ever learns that I sat on it for a month. The register is the evidence. It is not the conversation.
plain: Then entry 19 stays as it is, and nobody learns that I kept the information to myself for a month. The register is the evidence. It is not the discussion.

natural: I answered a questionnaire in March. I ticked four boxes and wrote the word fine. Ask me in this room and I will tell you what I told you on the twenty-seventh of April.
plain: I answered a questionnaire in March. I ticked four boxes and wrote the word fine. Ask me here, in this room, and I will tell you exactly what I told you on 27 April.

natural: Deming writes six headings on the board and does not sit down again for two hours. Scope and planning. Communication. Change control. Risk and issues. Acceptance and transition. The team.
plain: Deming writes six headings on the board. He does not sit down again for two hours. The headings are: scope and planning; communication; change control; risk and issues; acceptance and transition; the team.

natural: Change control. CR-014. Tell it so a stranger can use it.
plain: Change control. Change request CR-014. Describe it so that someone who was not here can use the lesson.

natural: A telephone call from a cabinet on the thirteenth of May 2027. Backstop screens in Release 2, please. Two days of everybody's life went into it before one word was written down.
plain: On 13 May 2027 someone from a Board member's private office telephoned. They asked for the backstop screens to be added to Release 2. We spent two days of everyone's time on it before anything was written down.

natural: Then it became a Change Request Form, a line in the Change Log, and a Steering Committee decision on the twenty-sixth. Postponed. Decision D-09.
plain: After that it became a Change Request Form, an entry in the Change Log, and a Steering Committee decision on 26 May 2027. The committee postponed it. The decision is recorded as D-09.

natural: One sentence for the stranger. A verbal scope request buys no estimating effort until it is on a form. It cost us two days. Somebody else can have it free.
plain: The lesson in one sentence. Do not spend any estimating effort on a spoken request for extra scope until it is written on a form. Those two days cost us money. Someone else can have the lesson for nothing.

natural: There is a second one underneath it, and it is not a change lesson. The cabinets were never on the Stakeholder Matrix. Nobody puts them there, because nobody thinks of them as stakeholders until one of them telephones.
plain: There is a second lesson underneath that one, and it is not about change control. The private offices were never listed in the Project Stakeholder Matrix. Nobody lists them, because nobody treats them as stakeholders until one of them telephones.

natural: Category stakeholder management. Recommendation: map the cabinets from Initiating, and give them a route that is not the telephone.
plain: I will file that under stakeholder management. The recommendation is: list the private offices as stakeholders from the Initiating Phase, and give them a way to ask for things that is not a telephone call.

natural: Risk.
plain: Next heading. Risk.

natural: R-07. Loss of a key architect. In the Risk Log since June 2026, strategy Reduce. Two actions: a key-person clause in the Levallois contract, and Nikola shadowing the design authority.
plain: Risk R-07: losing a key architect. It was in the Risk Log from June 2026. The chosen strategy was Reduce. There were two actions: a key-person clause in the Levallois contract, and Nikola Tesla working alongside the design authority so that he would know the same things.

natural: The clause worked. Our platform architect resigned in April 2027 and you had a named replacement and three weeks of handover, because the contract said so and because you paid for that sentence in 2026.
plain: The clause worked. Our platform architect resigned in April 2027. You received a named replacement and three weeks of handover, because the contract required it, and because you paid for that sentence in 2026.

natural: And in October we lost Nikola, and there was no clause, because he was the clause.
plain: Then in October 2027 we lost Nikola Tesla. No contract clause covered that, because he himself was the other half of our protection.

natural: Half our response to key-person risk was a person. We wrote one half into a contract and never wrote the other half down anywhere.
plain: Half of our answer to key-person risk was a person. We wrote one half into a contract. We never wrote the other half down anywhere.

natural: That is usable. We managed the risk well is not.
plain: That lesson can be used by others. The sentence we managed the risk well cannot.

natural: His last entry is still in the register. Twenty-two. We designed the migration to be run once, correctly. We ran it four times. Design it to be run twenty times.
plain: Nikola Tesla's last entry is still in the register. It is number 22. It says: we designed the data migration to be run once and to be correct. We ran it four times. Design it so it can be run twenty times.

natural: He wrote that in the week he left. It is the only polite thing he wrote that month.
plain: He wrote that in the week he left. It is the only polite thing he wrote in that whole month.

natural: Issues and conflict.
plain: Next heading. Issues and conflict.

natural: Ours, then. Whether retraining forty administrators lived in the Transition Plan or the Business Implementation Plan. Three weeks of 2026, and not politely.
plain: Then I will take this one. We argued about whether the retraining of 40 administrators belonged in the Transition Plan or in the Business Implementation Plan. The argument lasted three weeks in 2026 and it was not polite.

natural: It was mine to lose and I lost it correctly. It went into the Business Implementation Plan, under Grace, with Florence accountable. What a stranger should hear is that the argument was worth having in Planning, because afterwards it never once needed change control.
plain: It was my argument to lose, and I lost it for the right reason. The retraining went into the Business Implementation Plan, run by Grace Hopper, with Florence Nightingale accountable. The lesson for others is this: the argument was worth having during Planning. After that it never needed a change request.

natural: Acceptance. Marie.
plain: Next heading. Acceptance. Marie, please.

natural: The twenty-seventh of April. Nine hundred and ninety-eight loans reconciled and two did not, in the week of a three billion euro rollover. I refused. Somebody told me there was a process for refusing and, to my surprise, there was.
plain: On 27 April 2028, 998 loans matched and 2 did not. It was the week of a 3 billion euro bond rollover. I refused to accept the report. Someone told me there was a formal process for refusing. To my surprise, there was.

natural: My lesson is small. Acceptance criteria have to be written by somebody who does the job. Mine were, because I made a nuisance of myself in 2026. If I had not, I would have had nothing to refuse against, and I would have signed.
plain: My lesson is a small one. Acceptance criteria must be written by a person who does the work. Mine were, because I insisted on it in 2026. If I had not insisted, I would have had no criterion to measure against, and I would have signed.

natural: Last heading. What happens after us.
plain: Last heading. What should happen after this project ends.

natural: Three things. Benefit measurement across the 2029 reporting year. A follow-up project to onboard the backstop within six weeks of ratification, reusing the configuration engine and re-estimating CR-014 rather than re-opening it. And two product templates deferred out of Release 1, which are maintenance and not a project.
plain: Three things. First, measure the benefits across the whole 2029 reporting year. Second, a follow-up project to add the backstop instrument within six weeks of the treaty change being approved, reusing the configuration engine and making a new estimate for CR-014 instead of re-opening the old one. Third, two product templates that were left out of Release 1. Those are maintenance work, not a project.

natural: Grouped, in that order, and sent to every project manager in this building. Not filed.
plain: Group them in that order and send them to every project manager in this building. Do not simply file them.

natural: Count. Eleven of this afternoon's lessons were already in the register. Nine are new. Eight of the nine exist because two people contradicted each other in this room.
plain: Here is the count. 11 of this afternoon's lessons were already in the register. 9 are new. 8 of those 9 exist only because two people disagreed with each other in this room.

natural: Then the afternoon was worth it, and I will say so. It still does not tell me whether any of it was worth eight point nine six million.
plain: Then the afternoon was worth having, and I will say so. It still does not tell me whether the project was worth 8.96 million euro.

natural: Version zero point nine of the Project-End Report is open on the screen at section 2.1. Outside the plateau is white with heat and half the floor is already on leave.
plain: Version 0.9 of the Project-End Report is open on the screen at section 2.1. Outside it is very hot and bright. Half of the floor is already on holiday.

natural: Four of five met. Then, in the same paragraph, SC3 demonstrated but not yet proven in production. Read that to me as a Board member in October.
plain: The report says four of the five success criteria are met. Then, in the same paragraph, it says SC3 has been demonstrated but not proven in live use. Imagine you are a Board member reading that in October.

natural: It reads like what is true on the seventeenth of July. SC1, one working day, across fourteen disbursements. SC2, same-day reconciliation, every day. SC4, zero re-keyed fields since the fifteenth of May, from about fourteen hundred a quarter. SC5, both findings closed on the fourth.
plain: It reads like the truth on 17 July 2028. SC1: one working day, measured over 14 payments. SC2: reconciliation on the same day, every day. SC4: no fields typed again by hand since 15 May, down from about 1,400 every three months. SC5: both audit findings closed on 4 July.

natural: SC3 needs a new instrument and there is no new instrument. We configured one in a test environment in six weeks. That is a different claim and I am not writing it as the same one.
plain: SC3 needs a new lending product to set up, and there is no new lending product. We set one up in a test system in six weeks. That is a different statement, and I will not write it as if it were the same one.

natural: So. Four out of five with an asterisk.
plain: So it is four out of five, with a note attached.

natural: No. Four out of five today, and none of the five signed off, because signing them off takes a year. One working day across fourteen disbursements in a quiet July is not one working day across a quarter-end, an August and the week before Christmas.
plain: No. It is four out of five today, and none of the five is finally confirmed, because confirming them takes a year. One working day measured over 14 payments in a quiet July is not the same as one working day across a quarter end, an August, and the week before Christmas.

natural: Then I approve a report that says we do not know whether the project did what it was for.
plain: Then I approve a report which says that we do not know whether the project achieved its purpose.

natural: You approve a report that says what is true. Conclusions balanced, based on a thorough analysis of the facts. A report claiming what it cannot show is worse than one saying measurement continues, because the first kind is found out by somebody who was not in the room.
plain: You approve a report that says what is true. Conclusions must be balanced and based on a careful analysis of the facts. A report that claims what it cannot prove is worse than a report that says measurement is still going on. The first kind is discovered later by someone who was not here.

natural: And there is somewhere to put it. Section eight. One of the things that section is for, in the template's own words, is verifying that the intended benefits will be realised.
plain: And the report has a place for it. Section 8, Post-Project Recommendations. One purpose of that section, in the words of the template, is to check that the intended benefits will actually be achieved.

natural: Which is you handing it back to me.
plain: That means you are giving the problem back to me.

natural: To the permanent organisation. That happens to be you, but not as Project Owner. As Head of Lending Operations, with a system that has been in operations mode since May.
plain: I am giving it to the permanent organisation. That is you, but not in your role as Project Owner. It is you as Head of Lending Operations, with a system that has been in normal running since May.

natural: Guide page six. Chapter two, before any phase and before any artefact. Project outcomes and benefits are often realised only after the project has closed.
plain: This is on page 6 of the guide. It is in chapter 2, before any phase and before any document. It says that a project's outcomes and benefits often appear only after the project has closed.

natural: I said that sentence myself in Grace's office in 2026. I thought I was describing an inconvenience.
plain: I said that same sentence in Grace Hopper's office in 2026. At the time I thought I was describing a small problem.

natural: I will own the measurement. Quarterly, out of the Division's own operational reporting, from the third quarter of 2028. The full-year statement for 2029 goes to the Corporate Investment Board in the first quarter of 2030.
plain: I will take ownership of the measurement. It will be quarterly, taken from the Division's own operational reporting, starting with the third quarter of 2028. The statement for the whole of 2029 goes to the Corporate Investment Board in the first quarter of 2030.

natural: Named owner, named cadence, named date. Without those three, section eight is a wish with a heading on it.
plain: A named owner, a stated frequency and a fixed date. Without those three things, section 8 is only a hope with a title above it.

natural: Twenty-six months. Eight point nine six million. Forty people retrained. And the last sentence of it is that measurement continues.
plain: Twenty-six months. 8.96 million euro. 40 people retrained. And the final sentence is that measurement continues.

natural: The platform is the output. Straight-through processing is the outcome. The benefit is a number Grace reads in 2030. Three different things, and only the first was ever mine to finish.
plain: The platform is the output. Payments passing through without re-typing is the outcome. The benefit is a number that Grace Hopper will read in 2030. Those are three different things. Only the first one was ever mine to finish.

natural: It runs the other way as well. Nobody has ever thanked whoever built LOS, and close to three hundred billion euro went through it before we switched it off last month.
plain: It also works the other way. Nobody has ever thanked the people who built LOS. Almost 300 billion euro passed through that system before we switched it off last month.

natural: Say the rest of it. If the number is Grace's from August, then when it arrives it is not a verdict on anybody in this room.
plain: Say the rest of it. If the number belongs to Grace Hopper from August, then when the number arrives it is not a judgement on anyone in this room.

natural: No.
plain: No, it is not.

natural: I find I mind that less than I expected to.
plain: I am less unhappy about that than I expected to be.

natural: That is the sentence. Put it in 2.1 and again in section eight. Reports get read in fragments.
plain: That is the sentence to use. Put it in section 2.1 and again in section 8. People read reports in pieces, not from beginning to end.

natural: Write it so nobody reading it in 2031 can pretend they were promised numbers in July 2028.
plain: Write it so that nobody reading it in 2031 can claim they were promised results in July 2028.

natural: Sixteen fifty. She has one more question, and the way it is answered decides how the whole report is written.
plain: It is 16:50. She has one more question. The answer to it decides how the whole report will be written.

natural: Then draft it that way, and put Grace's name and Grace's dates in it rather than mine. If it is going to be somebody's job, the report should say whose.
plain: Then write it that way. Put Grace Hopper's name and Grace Hopper's dates in it, not mine. If it is going to be someone's job, the report should say whose job it is.

natural: On what budget? The cost centre stops on the thirty-first. And you would have me reporting to a project for eighteen months about a system I already operate.
plain: Paid from which budget? The cost centre closes on 31 July. And I would have to report to a project for eighteen months about a system that I already run.

natural: Then I do not review it, and I write to the Steering Committee saying why. Fourteen disbursements in July is not a statement about a reporting year, and a test configuration is not an onboarded instrument.
plain: Then I will not review it, and I will write to the Steering Committee to explain why. 14 payments in July say nothing about a whole reporting year. A test setup is not a real lending product in live use.

natural: Now you have gone the other way to feel honest about it. The system works. Marie stopped counting fields in May. Do not write me a defeat I did not have.
plain: Now you have gone too far in the other direction, so that you can feel honest. The system works. Marie Curie stopped counting re-typed fields in May. Do not write down a defeat that did not happen.

natural: The seventh floor. The room where Ready for Executing was decided, two years and twenty-two days ago, with the same green glare off the plateau. Lorenzo de' Medici has dialled in and will drop off at half past.
plain: This is the seventh floor. It is the room where the Ready for Executing gate was decided, two years and 22 days ago. The same green light comes off the glass outside. Lorenzo de' Medici has joined by telephone and will leave the call at 09:30.

natural: Item one, item two, and there is no item three. The Project-End Report, version one point zero, issued on the nineteenth. Twelve subjects, as the guidelines require. Effectiveness. Cost, schedule, scope and quality. Risk. Issues. Change. Communications. People and stakeholders. Acceptance. Business implementation and transition. The performance of the Core Team and of Levallois. Lessons learned. Post-project recommendations.
plain: There are two items on the agenda and no third one. The Project-End Report, version 1.0, was issued on 19 July 2028. It covers the twelve subjects the guide requires: effectiveness; cost, schedule, scope and quality; risk; issues; change; communications; people and stakeholders; acceptance of deliverables; business implementation and transition; the performance of the Project Core Team and of Levallois; lessons learned; post-project recommendations.

natural: Reviewed on the twenty-second, which was a Saturday. Reviewed is not approved. Two different rows, and I am fond of mine.
plain: I reviewed it on 22 July, which was a Saturday. Reviewing is not approving. They are two different rows in the table, and I like mine.

natural: Then who approves it? I had assumed that was me.
plain: Then who approves the report? I thought that was my job.

natural: This committee. Page sixty-six. Steering Committee Accountable, Project Manager Responsible, Project Owner Consulted.
plain: This committee approves it. Page 66 of the guide: the Steering Committee is accountable, the Project Manager is responsible, and the Project Owner is consulted.

natural: Consulted. On the report about my own project.
plain: So I am only consulted on the report about my own project.

natural: Yes. Your row changes on Friday. And on Friday you are the only person in the institution who can do the thing that has to be done.
plain: Yes. Your row in the table changes on Friday. On Friday you are the only person in this institution who can do what has to be done then.

natural: And me? What am I on this.
plain: And what about me? What is my role here?

natural: Informed. On all three Closing activities.
plain: You are informed. That is true for all three Closing activities.

natural: Good. I want it for the portfolio review in October and I would rather not be asked to approve a thing in order to be allowed to read it.
plain: Good. I want the report for the portfolio review in October. I do not want to be asked to approve something just so that I am allowed to read it.

natural: And the cost centre. Eight point nine six against eight point four, out of the administrative budget. Not one euro of it out of the lending capacity, whatever that newspaper printed in 2027. Close the line on the thirty-first.
plain: Now the cost centre. The project cost 8.96 million euro against a budget of 8.4 million. That money came from the administrative budget, which pays for running the institution. None of it came from the lending capacity, whatever a newspaper wrote in 2027. Close the budget line on 31 July.

natural: It closes on the thirty-first.
plain: The cost centre closes on 31 July 2028.

natural: Then I have nothing further. Delivered on the Charter date. I have approved considerably worse for considerably more.
plain: Then I have nothing more to say. The project delivered on the date in the Project Charter. I have approved much worse projects that cost much more.

natural: He leaves the call at nine seventeen without saying goodbye, which in this building is how contentment is expressed.
plain: He leaves the call at 09:17 without saying goodbye. In this building that is how people show they are satisfied.

natural: Can I ask the stupid question. Last time we sat in this room there was a gate and it had a name. What is this one called?
plain: May I ask a simple question. The last time we sat in this room there was a gate and it had a name. What is this one called?

natural: Nothing. There is no gate after Closing.
plain: It has no name. There is no gate after the Closing Phase.

natural: Three phase gates exist in PM². Ready for Planning at the end of Initiating. Ready for Executing at the end of Planning. Ready for Closing at the end of Executing. CASTOR passed the third on the twenty-second of June. There is no fourth.
plain: PM² has three phase gates. Ready for Planning at the end of Initiating. Ready for Executing at the end of Planning. Ready for Closing at the end of Executing. Project CASTOR passed the third gate on 22 June 2028. There is no fourth gate.

natural: That cannot be right. Something has to sign it dead.
plain: That cannot be correct. Something has to declare the project finished.

natural: Something does, and it is not a committee. There is a Closing sheet on the Phase-Exit Review Checklist. The last check asks whether the project is ready to be closed, and the answer does not travel to a gate. It travels to the Project Owner.
plain: Something does, and it is not a committee. The Phase-Exit Review Checklist has a sheet for Closing. The last question asks whether the project is ready to be closed. That answer does not go to a gate. It goes to the Project Owner.

natural: So the last event in a project is not permission to continue. It is permission to stop.
plain: So the last event in a project is not permission to go on. It is permission to stop.

natural: Which is why it feels like nothing. Every approval in twenty-six months opened a door.
plain: That is why it feels like nothing is happening. Every approval in the last 26 months opened a door.

natural: And this one shuts one, and nobody has written a ceremony for that.
plain: This one closes a door, and nobody has written a ceremony for closing a door.

natural: Then the part that is ours. The Project Steering Committee approves the Project-End Report of Project CASTOR, version one point zero, twenty-fifth of July 2028. Objections.
plain: Then let us do our part. The Project Steering Committee approves the Project-End Report of Project CASTOR, version 1.0, on 25 July 2028. Are there any objections?

natural: None. Henry Gantt reads the archive reference into the Minutes, which is the least ceremonious sentence anyone has spoken in this room all year.
plain: There are no objections. Henry Gantt reads the archive reference into the Minutes. It is the least ceremonial sentence anyone has spoken in this room all year.

natural: Twenty-six months, and it ends with a folder path.
plain: Twenty-six months of work, and it ends with the name of a folder.

natural: The folder path is the part that outlives us. In three years somebody starting a project none of us has thought of will read what Nikola wrote about running the migration four times, and it will save them a hundred days.
plain: The folder is the part that lasts longer than we do. In three years someone will start a project that none of us has imagined. They will read what Nikola Tesla wrote about running the migration four times, and it will save them 100 days.

natural: The second floor at the end of July, the building down to summer strength. The Project Support Office has a trolley in it and the trolley is full.
plain: It is the end of July on the second floor. Most staff are on holiday. There is a trolley in the Project Support Office and it is full of documents.

natural: Everything with CASTOR on it. Handbook, Work Plan, Stakeholder Matrix, four project-specific plans, six management plans, twenty-six Status Reports, two Progress Reports, six checklists, four logs, a hundred and ninety-one Minutes, and the Project-End Report. Folders 01 Initiating to 05 Closing, as we set them up in April 2026.
plain: This is everything with the name CASTOR on it. The Project Handbook, the Work Plan, the Stakeholder Matrix, four project-specific plans, six management plans, 26 Status Reports, 2 Progress Reports, 6 checklists, 4 logs, 191 sets of Minutes, and the Project-End Report. The folders run from 01 Initiating to 05 Closing, as we created them in April 2026.

natural: Your row, and the only support row in the phase. The Project Manager oversees closure and the release of resources. The Project Support Office assists in reviewing, organising and archiving.
plain: That is your row in the table, and it is the only support row in this phase. The Project Manager oversees the closure and the release of the people. The Project Support Office helps to review, organise and archive the documents.

natural: Document management. Seven years in the project space, classification applied to all of it. Two Status Reports had no version number and I have fixed them, which you may take as a general comment on May 2027.
plain: Now document management. The records are kept for seven years in the project space, and every document has a security classification. Two Status Reports had no version number. I have corrected them. You may treat that as a general comment about May 2027.

natural: Data protection. The parallel-run datasets held real counterparty and staff data. Deleted on Wednesday, certificate in folder 05. The record of processing activities now says the processing has ended. In four years an inspection reads that entry, not your system.
plain: Now data protection. The test data from the parallel run contained real information about borrowers and staff. It was deleted on Wednesday and the certificate is in folder 05. The record of processing activities now says that this processing has ended. In four years an inspection will read that entry, not your system.

natural: And LOS is off, but its data is not gone. Fourteen years of loan records keep their own retention clock, and from today that clock belongs to Lending Operations and not to a project that no longer exists.
plain: LOS is switched off, but its data still exists. Fourteen years of loan records must be kept for their own legal period. From today, that obligation belongs to the Lending Operations Division, not to a project that no longer exists.

natural: Security. LOS decommissioned on the thirtieth of June. Accounts closed, interfaces withdrawn, the two contractor accounts revoked on the fifteenth. The security file is closed and archived with the rest.
plain: Now information security. LOS was switched off for good on 30 June 2028. Its accounts are closed and its interfaces are withdrawn. The two contractor accounts were withdrawn on 15 July. The security file is closed and archived with everything else.

natural: Step one of Administrative Closure is that all documentation and records are reviewed, organised and archived. Nobody in the room calls it step one. It has taken nine working days.
