plain: Step 1 of Administrative Closure is to review, organise and archive all documents and records. Nobody in the room calls it step 1. The work has taken nine working days.

natural: Resources. Ada Lovelace went back to Lending Operations on the seventeenth. The two seconded architects return to the Levallois payroll on Monday, with the two contractor testers. The Project Core Team is dissolved on the thirty-first, and that is an act, not a feeling.
plain: Now the people. Ada Lovelace returned to Lending Operations on 17 July. The two architects lent to us go back onto the Levallois payroll on Monday, together with the two contractor test engineers. The Project Core Team is dissolved on 31 July. That is a formal act, not a feeling.

natural: The cost centre stops on the thirty-first.
plain: The cost centre closes on 31 July 2028.

natural: Say the last part again, slowly, for the people who are going to try.
plain: Please say that again slowly, for the people who will try to charge things anyway.

natural: Nothing can be charged to CASTOR after the thirty-first of July 2028.
plain: After 31 July 2028, nothing can be charged to Project CASTOR.

natural: Gustave Eiffel joins on the telephone for eight minutes, from somewhere with gulls in it.
plain: Gustave Eiffel joins by telephone for eight minutes. He is somewhere near the sea; you can hear seagulls.

natural: Contract side. Final invoice submitted on the twelfth, inside the payment terms. Retention releases against final acceptance, so it releases today or it does not release. Configuration and source in escrow under clause fourteen. Warranty runs to the fifteenth of May 2029 and defects go to your service desk, not to a project mailbox that will not exist.
plain: Now the contract. We sent the final invoice on 12 July, within the payment terms. The retention money is released when the project is finally accepted, so it is released today or not at all. The configuration and the source code are held in escrow under clause 14. The warranty runs until 15 May 2029. Faults go to your service desk, not to a project mailbox that will no longer exist.

natural: Step five. Verify that all contractual obligations have been fulfilled. Leonardo and I walked the Outsourcing Plan item by item this morning, with Gustave's list beside it.
plain: That is step 5: check that all obligations in the contract have been met. This morning Leonardo and I went through the Outsourcing Plan item by item, with Gustave Eiffel's list next to it.

natural: The warranty outliving the project bothered me for a week, until I understood it. It is not an open project. It is a contract, and contracts belong to operations.
plain: It worried me for a week that the warranty lasts longer than the project. Then I understood it. It is not an open project. It is a contract, and contracts belong to normal operations.

natural: For your file, then. A good project and a bad estimate, in that order. Do not let anyone print it the other way round.
plain: Then put this in your file. It was a good project and a bad estimate, in that order. Do not let anyone write it the other way round.

natural: You ride up with Deming at ten past three, because he wants to look at the floor that changed. The fourth-floor corridor is doing what it does in July, which is nothing at all.
plain: At 15:10 you go up in the lift with Deming, because he wants to see the floor that the project changed. The fourth-floor corridor is empty, as it always is in July.

natural: Do you know what is actually in that appendix at the back? The ethics one nobody reads.
plain: Do you know what is really in the appendix at the back of the guide? The one about ethics that nobody reads.

natural: Independence, impartiality, objectivity, loyalty.
plain: Independence, impartiality, objectivity and loyalty.

natural: Those are what you are meant to be. There are two more and they are the ones that do the work. Circumspection, which is stopping to think what a thing will cause. And responsibility, which is doing what you were given and looking for a way through when it will not go.
plain: Those four describe what you should be. There are two more, and they are the ones that do the real work. Circumspection means stopping to think about what an action will cause. Responsibility means doing the task you were given, and looking for a way through when it does not work.

natural: And the word for having both at once.
plain: And what is the word for having both of those at the same time?

natural: Integrity. It does not mean being agreeable. It means the same principles when they cost you something. Last week you told the Project Owner that four out of five was not four out of five. That cost you the best sentence in your own report.
plain: Integrity. It does not mean being pleasant. It means keeping the same principles when they cost you something. Last week you told the Project Owner that four out of five was not really four out of five. That cost you the best sentence in your own report.

natural: It was in the guide.
plain: It was written in the guide.

natural: Most of it is in the guide. That has never been the same thing as doing it.
plain: Most of it is written in the guide. Reading it has never been the same as doing it.

natural: Florence Nightingale is on leave from Saturday. Her assistant telephones at twenty past three. The Managing Director's office has taken her afternoon, and would the Project Manager sign the Project Acceptance Note so that she can countersign it in September.
plain: Florence Nightingale starts her holiday on Saturday. Her assistant telephones at 15:20. The Managing Director's office has taken her whole afternoon. She asks whether the Project Manager could sign the Project Acceptance Note now, so that she can add her signature in September.

natural: Ten minutes I have. Give me the note. And tell me in one sentence what I am signing, because I am not signing that the benefits arrived.
plain: I have ten minutes. Give me the note. Tell me in one sentence what I am signing, because I will not sign that the benefits have arrived.

natural: Then I file an archive that says the project closed on a day when the only person who could close it was on a beach. I will not file that.
plain: Then I would file an archive saying the project closed on a day when the only person who could close it was on holiday. I will not file that.

natural: Read the row again. It is the one row in the whole phase that moves. The Steering Committee is Consulted here, and Consulted has never been Accountable.
plain: Read the row again. It is the only row in this whole phase that changes. Here the Steering Committee is only consulted. Consulted has never meant accountable.

natural: Then you have released the only people who can answer a question about the folder, and left an archive nobody has approved. Those are the ones we are still chasing in 2031.
plain: Then you have released the only people who could answer a question about the folder, and you have left an archive that nobody approved. Those are the files we are still chasing in 2031.

natural: Rain over the Kirchberg plateau, the kind that hangs rather than falls. Not light yet. The fourth floor has been switched on since half past six.
plain: It is raining over Kirchberg. The rain hangs in the air rather than falling. It is still dark. The lights on the fourth floor have been on since 06:30.

natural: You are not here for CASTOR. There is a Project Initiation Request in your bag for something else entirely, dated Monday, and you have read it once. Grace Hopper has a chair pulled out already.
plain: You are not here for Project CASTOR. In your bag there is a Project Initiation Request for a completely different project. It is dated Monday and you have read it once. Grace Hopper has already pulled out a chair for you.

natural: Twenty minutes, then I have a rollover to prepare and you have a different problem to go and have.
plain: We have twenty minutes. After that I must prepare a bond rollover, and you must go and start a different problem.

natural: Third and fourth quarter of 2028, out of the Division's operational report and nothing of yours. SC1: one working day, forty-one disbursements, two of them on the thirty-first of December. SC2: same-day reconciliation, every day, including the week of the November rollover. SC4: zero re-keyed fields, from fourteen hundred a quarter.
plain: These are the figures for the third and fourth quarters of 2028. They come from the Division's own operational report, not from any project document. SC1: one working day, measured over 41 payments, two of them on 31 December. SC2: reconciliation on the same day, every day, including the week of the November rollover. SC4: no fields typed again by hand, down from about 1,400 every three months.

natural: SC5 stays closed unless Internal Audit reopens it. SC3 is still a blank line, because there is still no new instrument to onboard. And the full-year statement for 2029 goes to the Corporate Investment Board in February 2030, which is nineteen months after your cost centre closed.
plain: SC5 stays closed unless Internal Audit opens it again. SC3 is still empty, because there is still no new lending product to set up. The statement for the whole of 2029 goes to the Corporate Investment Board in February 2030. That is nineteen months after your project's cost centre closed.

natural: And it has not been your file since the twenty-eighth of July. That is not a complaint. It is the arrangement, and it was the right one.
plain: And it has not been your file since 28 July 2028. That is not a complaint. It is the agreement we made, and it was the right one.

natural: Henry Gantt comes off the lift with a laptop under one arm and the particular walk of somebody who has just found who he was looking for.
plain: Henry Gantt comes out of the lift with a laptop under one arm. He walks like a man who has just found the person he was looking for.

natural: The backstop onboarding project has had a project manager since the seventh. She pulled the CASTOR Project-End Report out of the archive on her second day, and she has a question I cannot answer.
plain: The backstop onboarding project has had a project manager since 7 January. On her second day she took the CASTOR Project-End Report out of the archive. She has a question that I cannot answer.

natural: She wants to know what it cost you to postpone CR-014, and whether she can simply re-open it.
plain: She wants to know what it cost you to postpone change request CR-014, and whether she can simply re-open it.

natural: Section 3.3 for why it happened, section 7 for what we learned from it, the Change Log for the money. A hundred and forty-five person-days and three hundred and ninety-two thousand at 2027 prices, against a data model that has changed twice since. Tell her to re-estimate, not to re-open.
plain: Section 3.3 explains why it happened. Section 7 gives what we learned. The Change Log has the money: 145 person-days and 392,000 euro at 2027 prices. The data model has changed twice since then. Tell her to make a new estimate, not to re-open the old one.

natural: So that is what the report was for.
plain: So that is the purpose of the report.

natural: It is the only thing it was ever for. Nobody writes one for the people who were in the room.
plain: That is the only purpose it ever had. Nobody writes a Project-End Report for the people who were in the room.

natural: Project Support Office. You will have heard that I am a Project Owner again. Same division, smaller project, and this time I read chapter eight before we started rather than after.
plain: Good morning, Project Support Office. You will have heard that I am a Project Owner again. It is the same division and a smaller project. This time I read chapter 8 of the guide before we started, not afterwards.

natural: In July I told you that a report which cannot state its benefits is a report admitting failure. I was wrong, and I have had six months to be wrong in. I do not intend to say it twice, so you will have to remember it for me.
plain: In July I told you that a report which cannot state its benefits is a report admitting failure. I was wrong, and I have had six months to think about it. I do not intend to say this a second time, so you will have to remember it for me.

natural: She asked for twenty minutes on how it goes. Not the artefacts. She has the artefacts, they are all in the archive. How it goes.
plain: The new project manager asked for twenty minutes on how a project goes. She does not need the documents. She has the documents; they are all in the archive. She wants to know how it goes.

natural: Somebody asks for something. You write down the ask, then the case for doing it at all, then the charter that says what it actually is, and somebody senior lets you plan. That is the first gate.
plain: Someone asks for something. You write down the request. Then you write the case for doing it at all. Then you write the charter, which says what the project really is. Then a senior person allows you to plan. That is the first gate.

natural: Then you plan it properly, and discover that the four plans everyone forgets are approved by four different people and none of them by you. That is the second gate.
plain: Then you plan it properly. You discover that the four plans everyone forgets are approved by four different people, and that none of them is approved by you. That is the second gate.

natural: Then you build it for two years, and every month you do the same small things. Report. Changes. Risks. Issues. Quality. Acceptance. Transition. The business side. Until the thing is in operation and the users have it in their hands. That is the third gate, and it is the last one.
plain: Then you build it for two years. Every month you do the same small things: reporting, changes, risks, issues, quality, acceptance, transition, and the business side. You continue until the system is live and the users have it. That is the third gate, and it is the last one.

natural: Then you stop. You sit in a hot room and say out loud what you would do differently, you write it down for people you will never meet, you give everything to the archive, and the Project Owner signs. There is no fourth gate. Nobody comes and tells you that you were right.
plain: Then you stop. You sit in a hot room and say aloud what you would do differently. You write it down for people you will never meet. You give everything to the archive. Then the Project Owner signs. There is no fourth gate. Nobody comes and tells you that you were right.

natural: And the benefits?
plain: And what about the benefits?

natural: About a year later, in somebody else's report, on a floor you no longer work on. That is not the sad part. That is the shape of the thing.
plain: They arrive about a year later, in someone else's report, on a floor where you no longer work. That is not the sad part. That is simply the shape of a project.

natural: If the three of you have finished. Florence asked me in July whether it works. I said January.
plain: If the three of you have finished talking. In July Florence Nightingale asked me whether the system works. I said she should ask me in January.

natural: It works.
plain: It works.

natural: And the honest version, which nobody asked for. The reconciliation is right every morning, including the two mornings I was certain it would not be. And two of my colleagues do a smaller job than they did in 2027, and one of them minds very much. Both of those are true, and only one of them will ever be in a report.
plain: And here is the honest version, which nobody asked for. The reconciliation is correct every morning, including the two mornings when I was sure it would not be. And two of my colleagues now do a smaller job than they did in 2027, and one of them is very unhappy about it. Both things are true. Only one of them will ever appear in a report.

natural: Now come here. There is something you have never actually watched.
plain: Now come here. There is something that you have never actually watched.

natural: On her screen, a disbursement to a programme country. Value date Monday. She types it once. The treasury system already has it, the payment gateway already has it, and she is done before the coffee arrives. Forty seconds, and nobody in this building will ever count them again.
plain: On her screen there is a payment to a programme country. The money must be in the account on Monday. She types it once. The treasury system already has it. The payment gateway already has it. She finishes before the coffee arrives. It takes 40 seconds, and nobody in this building will ever count those seconds again.
